_meta.purpose: DORA control catalogue in CatalogFile shape, so applyCatalogFile creates the framework, its requirements, the templates, their requirement links and the pack together.
_meta.why: These 24 templates and their 133 authored tasks reached no production database. The templates were created only by prisma/seed.ts, which is not run on production deploys, so the task seeder that names this fixture found nothing to attach to and reported "24 template(s) absent" on every run while exiting 0.
_meta.grounding: Requirement codes, titles and sections are carried over verbatim from prisma/fixtures/dora_requirements.json. Task content is unchanged from the bare-array fixture it replaces — this file is a shape conversion, not a re-authoring.
_meta.join: Every template.requirementCodes entry equals a requirement code exactly (24/24 resolve). The key rename matters: CatalogTemplateSchema reads requirementCodes and defaults it to [], so leaving the old `requirements` key would have parsed cleanly and produced 24 templates linked to nothing.

framework.name: Digital Operational Resilience Act
framework.description: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 on digital operational resilience for the financial sector.

requirements.title: Governance and organisation
requirements.summary: The management body defines, approves, oversees and is accountable for the ICT risk management framework, allocating clear roles and responsibilities for all ICT-related functions. (Paraphrase — Art. 5)

requirements.title: ICT risk management framework
requirements.summary: Maintain a sound, comprehensive and well-documented ICT risk management framework as part of the overall risk management system, reviewed at least annually. (Paraphrase — Art. 6)

requirements.title: ICT systems, protocols and tools
requirements.summary: Use and maintain ICT systems, protocols and tools that are reliable, have sufficient capacity, and are technologically resilient. (Paraphrase — Art. 7)

requirements.title: Identification
requirements.summary: Identify, classify and document all ICT-supported business functions, information assets and ICT assets, and map dependencies. (Paraphrase — Art. 8)

requirements.title: Protection and prevention
requirements.summary: Continuously monitor and control ICT systems, and implement policies, procedures and tools (access control, encryption, network security) to protect against ICT risk. (Paraphrase — Art. 9)

requirements.title: Detection
requirements.summary: Have mechanisms to promptly detect anomalous activities, including ICT network performance issues and ICT-related incidents, with multiple layers of control and defined alert thresholds. (Paraphrase — Art. 10)

requirements.title: Response and recovery
requirements.summary: Put in place a comprehensive ICT business continuity policy and response-and-recovery plans to ensure continuity of critical functions and limit damage. (Paraphrase — Art. 11)

requirements.title: Backup policies, restoration and recovery procedures
requirements.summary: Develop and document backup policies and restoration/recovery procedures, with backups stored securely and recovery tested periodically. (Paraphrase — Art. 12)

requirements.title: Learning and evolving
requirements.summary: Gather information on vulnerabilities, ICT-related incidents and cyber threats, conduct post-incident reviews, and feed lessons learned back into the framework. (Paraphrase — Art. 13)

requirements.title: Communication
requirements.summary: Have crisis communication plans enabling responsible disclosure of major ICT-related incidents to clients, counterparts and the public as appropriate. (Paraphrase — Art. 14)

requirements.title: Simplified ICT risk management framework
requirements.summary: Certain smaller and non-interconnected entities apply a simplified but still sound ICT risk management framework proportionate to their risk profile. (Paraphrase — Art. 16)

requirements.title: ICT-related incident management process
requirements.summary: Define, establish and implement an ICT-related incident management process to detect, manage, log and resolve ICT-related incidents. (Paraphrase — Art. 17)

requirements.title: Classification of ICT-related incidents and cyber threats
requirements.summary: Classify ICT-related incidents and determine their impact using the criteria set out in DORA and the related RTS (clients affected, duration, geographical spread, data losses, criticality, economic impact). (Paraphrase — Art. 18)

requirements.title: Reporting of major ICT-related incidents and voluntary notification of significant cyber threats
requirements.summary: Report major ICT-related incidents to the relevant competent authority through an initial notification, an intermediate report and a final report within the deadlines set by DORA and its RTS/ITS. (Paraphrase — Art. 19)

requirements.title: Operational or security payment-related incidents
requirements.summary: Credit institutions, payment institutions, account information service providers and electronic money institutions apply the incident provisions to operational or security payment-related incidents. (Paraphrase — Art. 23)

requirements.title: General requirements for the performance of digital operational resilience testing
requirements.summary: Establish a risk-based digital operational resilience testing programme as an integral part of the ICT risk management framework. (Paraphrase — Art. 24)

requirements.title: Testing of ICT tools and systems
requirements.summary: Perform an appropriate range of tests on ICT systems and tools — including vulnerability assessments, scans, gap analyses, penetration testing and scenario-based tests — at least yearly on critical systems. (Paraphrase — Art. 25)

requirements.title: Advanced testing of ICT tools, systems and processes based on TLPT
requirements.summary: Identified financial entities carry out threat-led penetration testing (TLPT) on live production systems covering critical functions at least every three years. (Paraphrase — Art. 26)

requirements.title: Requirements for testers for the carrying out of TLPT
requirements.summary: Use testers for TLPT that meet suitability, independence and professional-ethics requirements, with appropriate certification or accreditation. (Paraphrase — Art. 27)

requirements.title: General principles (incl. Register of Information)
requirements.summary: Manage ICT third-party risk as part of the ICT risk framework, adopt a strategy on ICT third-party risk, and maintain a Register of Information on all contractual arrangements for the use of ICT services. (Paraphrase — Art. 28)

requirements.title: Preliminary assessment of ICT concentration risk at entity level
requirements.summary: Assess ICT concentration risk when entering contractual arrangements for critical or important functions, including risks from sub-outsourcing and hard-to-substitute providers. (Paraphrase — Art. 29)

requirements.title: Key contractual provisions
requirements.summary: Ensure ICT service contracts contain the mandatory key contractual provisions (service descriptions, locations, data protection, access and audit rights, termination, exit support, incident assistance). (Paraphrase — Art. 30)

requirements.title: Designation of critical ICT third-party service providers
requirements.summary: Recognise that certain ICT third-party providers are designated as critical by the ESAs and become subject to the Union Oversight Framework; account for this in third-party risk management. (Paraphrase — Art. 31)

requirements.title: Information-sharing arrangements on cyber threat information and intelligence
requirements.summary: Financial entities may exchange cyber threat information and intelligence within trusted communities under arrangements that protect confidentiality, personal data and competition-sensitive information. (Paraphrase — Art. 45)

templates.title: ICT governance and management-body accountability
templates.description: Place every ICT function under a named owner and an accountable management body, and set out in policy how that body directs, approves and reviews ICT risk rather than delegating it away.
templates.objective: To ensure the management body directs and answers for ICT risk itself, with every ICT-related function tied to a named owner and an accountable member.
templates.successCriteria:
Every ICT-related function in the responsibilities matrix has an owning team and a named accountable management-body member.
The governance policy in force is the version the minutes record the management body as approving.
Each approval and periodic review of the ICT risk framework is minuted against a named framework version.
Every management-body member has ICT risk training recorded within the cycle.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the responsibilities matrix showing the owning team and accountable management-body member per ICT function.
Request the approved ICT governance policy with its version, approval date and approving body.
Collect the minute extracts recording management-body approval or review of the ICT risk framework.
Obtain the board ICT risk training records showing session, date and attendance per member.

Analysis:
Trace each ICT function in the organisation structure to a matrix row and confirm both an owner and an accountable member are named.
Confirm the policy version in force is the one the minutes approved, not a later revision issued without them.
Check each minuted item records a decision on a named framework version rather than noting the framework.
Compare training attendance with the current membership list and identify members with no session in the cycle.

Output:
Accountability coverage schedule marking each ICT function assigned, unassigned or disputed.
Findings note on the approval trail between the policy in force and the minutes approving it.
Exception list of management-body members without current ICT risk training, with each gap's age.

title.en: Map every ICT-related function to its owning team and its management-body accountability

description.en: Take the list of ICT-related functions the entity runs — ICT operations, security, change, resilience and third-party management — and record for each the team that performs it, the executive who owns delivery, and where accountability for it sits within the management body. One row per function, and no row left blank or carrying an accountability that cannot be traced to a current role holder. This matrix is what shows the management body has allocated clear roles and responsibilities for its ICT-related functions rather than leaving them unassigned. Attach the completed responsibilities matrix, dated and version-marked.

evidenceHint.en: Management body responsibilities matrix, one row per ICT-related function, recording the owning team and where management-body accountability sits

text.en: List every ICT-related function the entity operates, including those delivered by third parties.
Name the team that performs each function and the executive who owns its delivery.
Record where management-body accountability for each function listed sits.
Resolve any row left blank or naming an accountability with no current holder.
Date and version-mark the matrix, then table it at the management body for confirmation.

title.en: Publish the ICT governance policy setting how the management body approves and oversees the framework

description.en: Write the governance policy that records how the ICT risk management framework is defined, approved and overseen: which body approves it, what material that body is given before approving, how ICT risk reaches it between approvals, and how the responsibilities matrix is kept current when a role holder changes. State plainly that the management body remains accountable for the framework it approves. Route it through the entity's normal document-approval path and attach the approved version, carrying its version number and approval date.

evidenceHint.en: Approved ICT governance policy showing its version, approval date and approving body

title.en: Record each management-body approval and periodic review of the ICT risk framework in the minutes

description.en: Every time the management body approves the ICT risk management framework or takes it back for periodic review, minute the version considered, the material it was given, the decision reached, and any actions raised with their owners and dates. A minute saying only that the framework was noted evidences neither approval nor review — the decision has to be named. Attach the minute extract covering the period together with the framework version it refers to.

evidenceHint.en: Minute extract recording the management body's approval or review decision, naming the framework version considered

title.en: Log the ICT-risk training and briefings delivered to each management-body member

description.en: Record, per management-body member, the ICT-risk training or briefing they received during the period: the session, its date, who delivered it, and the subjects covered. Where a member did not attend, record the catch-up arranged and when it took place. HR schedules the sessions and captures attendance; accountability sits with the management body itself, which the framework expects to hold sufficient ICT-risk knowledge to challenge what it is shown. Attach the training record for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Board ICT risk training records showing the session, date and attendance for each management-body member

title.en: Verify that every ICT function in the responsibilities matrix still has a named accountable member

description.en: Check the responsibilities matrix against the current management body and executive population: every function still carries a named accountable member, no departed or reassigned individual remains, and any ICT function created since the last check appears. Record each gap found, the person now accountable, and the date the matrix was corrected. Attach the checked matrix with the list of changes made.

evidenceHint.en: Checked responsibilities matrix with the list of gaps found, the reassignments made and the dates corrected

text.en: Pull the current management-body and executive role holders from the HR record.
Flag every matrix row whose named individual has left or changed role.
Identify ICT functions created since the last check and add the missing rows.
Record the new accountable member for each gap and the date the row was corrected.

templates.title: ICT risk management framework
templates.description: Hold the ICT risk management framework as a single document with a stated scope and a declared link to the entity's overall risk management, so ICT risk is governed as part of the whole rather than beside it.
templates.objective: To ensure ICT risk is governed within the entity's overall risk management, through one framework document and a resilience strategy that carries funding.
templates.successCriteria:
The scope statement names the entities, functions and ICT services covered and its line into overall risk management.
One controlled framework document is in force, versioned and owned, with no competing copy in circulation.
The resilience strategy sets objectives with planned activities, a measure of progress and an approved budget against each.
The framework was reviewed within the year and again after each major ICT-related incident.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the scope statement listing covered entities, functions and ICT services and its reporting line into overall risk management.
Request the ICT risk management framework document with its version, owner and approval date.
Collect the digital operational resilience strategy with its objectives, planned activities and progress measures.
Obtain the budget allocation record by activity and the annual and post-incident review records.

Analysis:
Compare the scope statement with the entity's legal structure and ICT service list for functions covered by neither the framework nor an exclusion.
Search the policy store for competing or superseded framework copies still being relied on.
Check each strategy objective has a planned activity and a measure by which progress on it can be judged.
Reconcile budgeted activities with strategy activities and list those planned with no approved funding.
Read the review record for the version reviewed, the changes made and the reasons given for items left unchanged.

Output:
Scope coverage table naming functions and ICT services attributed to no part of the framework.
Strategy-to-budget reconciliation separating funded from unfunded resilience activities.
Review timeliness record giving the interval since the last review and the status of each major incident.

title.en: Define the scope of the ICT risk framework and its link to the overall risk management system

description.en: Write down what the ICT risk management framework covers — which legal entities, business functions and ICT services — and how it sits inside the entity's overall risk management system: the risk taxonomy it uses, where ICT risk is reported into enterprise risk, and which existing risk policies it inherits from rather than restates. Name what is deliberately out of scope and the reason. Attach the scope statement, issued with the framework document it governs.

evidenceHint.en: Scope statement listing the entities, functions and ICT services covered, and the reporting line into the overall risk management system

text.en: List the legal entities, business functions and ICT services the framework covers.
Record the risk taxonomy and rating scale the framework will use throughout.
State where ICT risk is reported into the overall risk management system.
Name anything deliberately excluded from scope and the reason for excluding it.
Issue the scope statement alongside the framework document it governs.

title.en: Document the ICT risk management framework as a single controlled document

description.en: Bring the framework's parts into one controlled document rather than a set of cross-references: the ICT risk taxonomy, the assessment method and rating scale, the roles that operate it, the control set it relies on, the risk-acceptance route, and the reporting lines into enterprise risk. Give it a version number, a named owner and an approval date so a later reviewer can tell which version was in force when. Attach the approved framework document.

evidenceHint.en: ICT risk management framework document, versioned, owned and carrying its approval date

text.en: Draft the ICT risk taxonomy and the rating scale applied to each risk.
Record the assessment method and the roles that perform each step of it.
Set out the risk-acceptance route and who may accept an ICT risk.
Name the control set the framework relies on and where it is described.
Assign a version number, a document owner and an approval date.

title.en: Publish the digital operational resilience strategy setting how ICT risk will be addressed

description.en: Write the strategy that states how the entity intends to address ICT risk and meet its digital operational resilience objectives: the objectives themselves, the methods chosen to reach them, the resilience activities planned for the period, and how progress against each is measured. Reference the framework document for method rather than repeating it, so the two cannot drift apart. Attach the approved strategy with the objectives and planned activities visible.

evidenceHint.en: Approved digital operational resilience strategy listing the resilience objectives, planned activities and the measures of progress

title.en: Record the resilience budget approved for the period against each planned activity

description.en: Take the activities the digital operational resilience strategy commits to for the period and record the budget approved against each one, alongside what has actually been spent or committed. Where a committed activity carries no budget, record that gap and where it was escalated — an unfunded commitment is the finding this task exists to surface. Attach the budget allocation record together with evidence of its approval.

evidenceHint.en: Budget allocation record showing the approved digital operational resilience budget by activity, with the approval and the spend to date

title.en: Review the ICT risk framework annually and again after each major ICT-related incident

description.en: Run the review the framework itself requires: at least annually, and again following any major ICT-related incident. Record what was examined, what changed in the framework as a result, and what was deliberately left unchanged with the reason. A review producing no record is indistinguishable from one that never ran, so the record is the deliverable rather than the discussion. Attach the review record naming the framework version before and after.

evidenceHint.en: Annual review record naming the framework version reviewed, the changes made and the items left unchanged with their reasons

text.en: Confirm which trigger applies — the annual cycle or a major ICT-related incident.
Examine the framework against the risks and incidents seen since the last review.
Record each change made to the framework and the reason it was made.
Record the items considered and deliberately left unchanged, with the reasoning.
Issue the revised framework version and note it in the review record.

templates.title: ICT systems, protocols and tools
templates.description: State the capacity and reliability each ICT system must meet and the architecture standards its protocols and tools must satisfy, so a system's fitness is judged against a written expectation.
templates.objective: To hold each ICT system to a written capacity, reliability and architecture expectation, so unfit or out-of-support technology is found before it fails in service.
templates.successCriteria:
Every in-scope ICT system has capacity and reliability requirements traceable to the function it serves and a stated volume source.
Architecture standards are published with a deviation route and a named authority who may grant one.
Observed peak utilisation stays within each system's recorded headroom, or the exceedance is raised in the capacity plan.
Every ICT tool and protocol shows a running version and end-of-support date, with out-of-support entries owned.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the capacity and reliability requirements schedule with the function served and volume source per system.
Request the approved architecture standards with their deviation route and grant authority.
Collect the capacity plan showing observed peak utilisation against each system's recorded headroom.
Obtain the technology currency record giving running version, supported version and end-of-support date per tool.
Obtain the latest architecture standards assessment with its deviation list and owners.

Analysis:
Sample the asset inventory and confirm each system appears in the schedule with a volume source that can be followed to origin.
Compare observed peak utilisation with recorded headroom and list systems that ran beyond it with no action raised.
Test the currency record against vendor support dates and identify tools still running past end-of-support.
Check each architecture deviation was granted by the named authority and carries an owner, not an open status alone.

Output:
Requirements coverage list marking systems with no recorded capacity or reliability figure.
Out-of-support technology register with an owner and remediation date per entry.
Deviation ageing report drawn from successive architecture standards assessments.

title.en: Record the capacity and reliability requirements each ICT system must meet

description.en: For every ICT system supporting a business operation, write down the volume it must carry at peak, the availability it is expected to hold, and the headroom the entity intends to keep above observed demand. Derive the figures from the scale of the operations the system actually supports, not from the vendor's published specification, and record against each row the business function it serves and where the volume figures came from. Attach the requirements schedule, one row per system.

evidenceHint.en: Capacity and reliability requirements schedule, one row per ICT system, naming the business function served and the source of the volume figures

text.en: List the ICT systems supporting each business operation in scope.
Record the peak transaction or user volume each system has to carry.
Record the availability the business function requires of that system.
State the capacity headroom to be held above observed peak demand.
Record for each row the business function served and the source of its figures.

title.en: Publish the architecture standards ICT systems, protocols and tools must be built to

description.en: Set out the standards a new or changed ICT system, protocol or tool has to meet before it is put into use: supported protocol versions, redundancy expectations, the capacity headroom carried over from the requirements schedule, and the technology-currency rule the entity applies to versions and support dates. State how a deviation is requested, who may grant one, and how long a granted deviation lasts. Attach the approved architecture standards.

evidenceHint.en: Approved architecture standards, including the deviation route and who may grant one

title.en: Record observed utilisation against each ICT system's capacity headroom in the capacity plan

description.en: For the period, take the observed peak utilisation of each ICT system and record it in the capacity plan beside the requirement set for that system. Flag every system whose remaining headroom has fallen below the level in the requirements schedule, name the action agreed, and give it an owner. A plan carrying only forecasts and no observed figures cannot show whether capacity was ever sufficient. Attach the updated capacity plan for the period.

evidenceHint.en: ICT asset capacity plan for the period showing observed peak utilisation against each system's recorded headroom

text.en: Collect observed peak utilisation for each system over the period.
Enter each figure in the capacity plan beside that system's requirement.
Flag systems whose headroom has fallen below the recorded level.
Record the agreed action and owner for each flagged system.

title.en: Record the running version and end-of-support date of every ICT tool and protocol

description.en: Work through the ICT tools, protocols and platforms in the asset inventory and record for each the version actually running, the version the vendor currently supports, and the date support ends. Mark every entry already past that date or due to pass it before the next check, and name who owns the upgrade. Attach the technology currency record for the period with the out-of-support entries listed separately.

evidenceHint.en: Technology currency record listing running version, supported version and end-of-support date per ICT tool, with the out-of-support entries called out

title.en: Assess each in-scope ICT system against the architecture standards and list the deviations

description.en: Take the architecture standards and check each in-scope ICT system against them clause by clause, recording whether the system conforms, deviates under a granted exception, or deviates with no exception at all. The last group is the finding: give each one an owner and a remediation date. Attach the assessment together with its deviation list and the exceptions relied on.

evidenceHint.en: Architecture standards assessment with the deviation list, the exceptions relied on and a named owner per unremediated deviation

text.en: Select the in-scope ICT systems and the standards clauses each must meet.
Record per clause whether the system conforms or deviates from the standard.
Match each deviation against the register of granted exceptions.
Assign an owner and a remediation date to every deviation with no exception.

templates.title: Asset and dependency identification
templates.description: Keep one register of every ICT and information asset, classify each ICT-supported business function by criticality with the basis recorded, and map the dependencies each function relies on.
templates.objective: To ensure the entity knows what ICT it holds, which business functions are critical, and what each of those functions actually depends on to keep running.
templates.successCriteria:
One register holds every ICT and information asset, including those a third party operates on the entity's behalf.
Each ICT-supported business function has a criticality rating with its basis recorded and the rater named.
Every critical function is mapped to the assets and providers it depends on, with unresolved dependencies listed rather than omitted.
Additions, changes and retirements appear in the change log, and discovery discrepancies are resolved in both directions.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the dated ICT asset inventory covering ICT and information assets, including third-party operated ones.
Request the criticality mapping showing the rating, its stated basis and who set it per business function.
Collect the dependency map linking critical functions to their assets and third-party providers.
Obtain the inventory change log for the period and the register-to-discovery comparison.

Analysis:
Compare the register with network discovery or the procurement ledger and quantify assets present in one and missing from the other.
Sample service-provider contracts and check whether the assets they operate appear in the register at all.
Test a sample of criticality ratings to see whether the rating follows from the basis recorded for it.
Trace each critical function to its dependency entry and identify mapping that stops at the application layer.

Output:
Inventory completeness measure naming the populations compared and discrepancies found in each direction.
Criticality sampling results listing ratings unsupported by their stated basis.
Dependency gap list naming critical functions with incomplete or unresolved mapping.

title.en: Inventory every ICT asset and information asset in a single register

description.en: Build one register covering ICT assets and information assets alike: what the asset is, who owns it, which business function it supports, where it runs, and — for information assets — the class of data it holds. Include assets operated on the entity's behalf by an ICT third-party provider: an asset is in scope because the entity depends on it, not because the entity hosts it. Attach the register, dated and version-marked.

evidenceHint.en: ICT asset inventory covering ICT and information assets, including those operated by third parties, dated and version-marked

text.en: Pull the current asset population from each source system you already hold.
Add the assets operated on the entity's behalf by ICT third-party providers.
Record the owner and the business function supported for every asset.
Record the data class held for each information asset in the register.
Date and version-mark the register before circulating it for use.

title.en: Classify each ICT-supported business function by criticality and record the basis for the rating

description.en: Apply one criticality scale to every ICT-supported business function and record, per function, the rating given and the reasoning behind it — the impact of losing the function, who is affected, and the tolerance the business itself states. A rating with no stated basis cannot be challenged or reused by anyone else, so the reasoning is part of the deliverable rather than a note. Attach the criticality mapping, recording who set each rating and when.

evidenceHint.en: Business-function criticality mapping showing the rating, the stated basis and who set it for each ICT-supported function

text.en: Agree the criticality scale and what each level means in practice.
Rate every ICT-supported business function against that single scale.
Record the impact, the affected parties and the tolerance behind each rating.
Record who set each rating, the date it was set and the basis given.

title.en: Map each critical business function to the ICT assets and third parties it depends on

description.en: Trace every function rated critical down to the ICT assets that deliver it and outward to the ICT third-party providers those assets rely on, including any onward dependency the provider itself names. Record each link in both directions so a single asset's loss can be read back to the functions it would stop. Attach the dependency map together with the list of functions it covers and any dependency that could not be established.

evidenceHint.en: ICT dependency map linking critical business functions to their assets and third-party providers, with unresolved dependencies listed

text.en: Select the business functions rated critical in the criticality mapping.
Trace each function down to the ICT assets that actually deliver it.
Extend each asset outward to the ICT third-party providers it relies on.
Record the onward dependencies those providers name in their own answers.
List separately any dependency that could not be established, with the reason.

title.en: Record every asset addition, change and retirement in the inventory as it occurs

description.en: Keep the register current at the point of change rather than at review time: when an asset is commissioned, moved, re-owned or retired, record what changed, the date, and who made the change. Retired assets stay in the register marked retired, so a dependency map drawn later still resolves against them. Attach a dated export of the register for the period together with its change log.

evidenceHint.en: Dated ICT asset inventory export for the period with the change log showing additions, changes and retirements

title.en: Verify the asset register against an independent discovery source and record the discrepancies

description.en: Compare the register against an independent view of what is actually running — a discovery scan, a cloud account listing, or a provider's own inventory — and record what appears in one and not the other, in both directions. An asset present in the register but absent in reality is as much a finding as the reverse. Assign every discrepancy an owner and record how it was resolved. Attach the comparison with its discrepancy list.

evidenceHint.en: Register-to-discovery comparison listing each discrepancy in both directions, its owner and its resolution

text.en: Select the independent discovery source for each part of the estate.
Compare the register against that source in both directions.
Record assets found in reality but missing from the register.
Record register entries with no corresponding asset in reality.
Assign an owner to each discrepancy and record how it was resolved.

templates.title: Protection and prevention controls
templates.description: Record which protection controls apply to each ICT system and data holding, and publish the access control policy governing how ICT access is granted, approved and withdrawn.
templates.objective: To ensure each ICT system and data holding has stated protection controls, and that deployed access, encryption and segmentation match the published standards.
templates.successCriteria:
Every ICT and information asset sits in the protection control coverage table, and each exclusion carries a written reason.
The access control policy names the systems it binds, the approver for each grant type and the record kept per grant.
Encryption standards fix algorithm, key length and key custody by data class, with departures on the deviation list.
Critical systems sit in segments with defined permitted flows, and every release carries its risk assessment and required approval.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the protection control coverage table mapping each asset to the controls applied, with reasons for exclusions.
Request the access control policy and the encryption standards with their current deviation list.
Collect the network configuration export showing segments, permitted flows and the function each segment serves.
Obtain the ICT change records for the period and the latest configuration conformance check.

Analysis:
Reconcile the coverage table with the asset inventory and identify assets in neither the covered nor the excluded population.
Sample access grants and test that the approver matched the grant type the policy requires and the record was kept.
Compare deployed cipher settings on sampled systems against the algorithm and key length the standards fix.
Inspect segment rules for flows reaching a critical system from general traffic with no defined permission behind them.
Test sampled releases for a risk assessment and named approval, and search for releases with no change record.

Output:
Coverage reconciliation naming unmapped assets and exclusions recorded without a reason.
Cryptographic and segmentation conformance findings against the published standards.
Change-approval exception schedule with an owner and remediation date per deviation.

title.en: Record which protection controls apply to each ICT system and data holding

description.en: Take the ICT and information asset population and mark, per asset, which of the entity's protection controls apply to it: identity and access management, encryption at rest, encryption in transit, network segregation, and change control. An asset carrying no control at all is either out of scope with a written reason or a gap to be raised. Attach the coverage table with the reason recorded against every exclusion.

evidenceHint.en: Protection control coverage table mapping each ICT and information asset to the controls that apply, with a written reason per exclusion

text.en: Take the asset population from the ICT and information asset register.
Mark which protection controls apply to each asset in the population.
Record a written reason against every asset excluded from a control.
Raise as a gap any asset carrying no protection control and no reason.

title.en: Publish the access control policy governing how ICT access is granted, approved and removed

description.en: Write the policy that states who may hold which access to ICT systems, who approves a grant, how privileged access is treated differently from ordinary access, and how access is withdrawn when a role changes or ends. Name the systems the policy binds and the record kept for each grant, so a later reviewer can test a grant against it. Attach the approved access control policy with its version and approval date.

evidenceHint.en: Approved access control policy naming the systems it binds, the approver for each grant type and the record kept per grant

title.en: Record the encryption standards applied to ICT data at rest and in transit

description.en: Write down, per data class in the asset register, what the entity requires at rest and in transit: the algorithm, the minimum key length, and where the keys are held. Where a system cannot meet the standard, record it as a deviation with the compensating control and a review date rather than lowering the standard to fit. Attach the approved encryption standards together with the deviation list.

evidenceHint.en: Approved encryption standards stating algorithm, minimum key length and key custody per data class, with the deviation list

text.en: List the data classes carried by the assets in the register.
Record the algorithm and minimum key length required at rest per class.
Record the algorithm and minimum key length required in transit per class.
State where the keys for each class are held and by whom.
List systems that cannot meet the standard with their compensating control.

title.en: Segment the network so critical ICT systems are isolated from general traffic

description.en: Place the systems supporting critical business functions into their own network segments and restrict what may reach them to the flows those functions actually need. Capture the resulting arrangement as an exported configuration — segment definitions, permitted flows and the rules enforcing them — rather than a hand-drawn diagram, so it can be compared against what is deployed. Attach the network security configuration export with the segment-to-function mapping.

evidenceHint.en: Network security configuration export showing segment definitions, permitted flows and the mapping of each segment to the critical function it serves

text.en: Identify the systems supporting each critical business function.
Assign those systems to segments separated from general traffic.
Record the flows each function genuinely needs into and out of its segment.
Restrict the enforcing rules to those flows and remove the remainder.
Export the resulting configuration and map each segment to its function.

title.en: Approve every ICT change through the documented change process before release

description.en: Run each change to an in-scope ICT system through the route the ICT change management policy sets: a raised request, an assessment of the ICT risk it carries, a recorded approval by the named approver, and a release record. Where the policy provides a separate emergency route, the record must show which route was used and why. Attach the change records for the period, including every change taken by the emergency route.

evidenceHint.en: ICT change records for the period, each carrying the risk assessment, the named approval required by the ICT change management policy and the release record

title.en: Verify that deployed access, encryption and segmentation settings match the published standards

description.en: Sample the systems in the coverage table and check what is actually configured against the access control policy, the encryption standards and the segmentation export — reading the live configuration, not the previous review's findings. Record every deviation with the system, the clause it fails, the owner and the remediation date. Attach the conformance check with its deviation list and the sample it was drawn from.

evidenceHint.en: Configuration conformance check listing the sample taken, each deviation from the published standards, its owner and remediation date

text.en: Draw a sample of systems from the protection control coverage table.
Read the live access configuration and compare it with the access control policy.
Read the live encryption settings and compare them with the encryption standards.
Compare the deployed segmentation rules against the exported configuration.
Record each deviation with its failing clause, owner and remediation date.

templates.title: Anomalous-activity detection
templates.description: Name the log sources and network segments detection must cover and the layer it operates at, and set an alert threshold and escalation trigger for each class of anomalous activity.
templates.objective: To ensure anomalous activity on in-scope systems and segments is detected at a defined threshold and reaches a named receiver, rather than resting in unread logs.
templates.successCriteria:
Every in-scope system and segment names a log or telemetry source and control layer, with uncollected sources marked as gaps.
Each anomaly type monitored has a firing value, a receiver and an escalation trigger in the threshold register.
Collection and an alerting rule are live for every row of the detection coverage list.
Alerts raised in the period each carry a triage outcome, and simulated events fire their rule and reach the recorded receiver.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the detection coverage list naming the log or telemetry source and control layer per system and segment.
Request the threshold register giving the firing value, receiver and escalation trigger per anomaly type.
Collect the monitoring and alerting configuration export mapped to the coverage rows it satisfies.
Obtain the log review procedure with the completed reviews, the alert triage record and the detection test results.

Analysis:
Compare the coverage list with the asset inventory and count systems and segments naming no collection source.
Select register rows and confirm a deployed rule exists at the same firing value in the configuration export.
Trace sampled alerts back to the threshold that fired them and forward to the escalation the register requires.
Test whether reviews recorded as finding nothing were performed, using reviewer identity and timestamps in the platform.
Read the detection test results for rules that failed to fire, fired late or reached the wrong receiver.

Output:
Detection coverage gap list naming the sources and segments not collected.
Threshold-to-rule reconciliation showing registered thresholds with no deployed rule.
Detection test summary stating the rules exercised and those that raised no alert.

title.en: Record the log sources and network segments detection must cover, and at which layer

description.en: List the systems, network segments and applications where anomalous activity has to be detectable, and against each name the log or telemetry source that would carry the evidence and the layer of control it sits at — endpoint, network, application or platform. Where a listed source is not currently collected, keep the row and mark it as a gap rather than dropping it. Attach the detection coverage list with its gaps identified.

evidenceHint.en: Detection coverage list naming the log or telemetry source and control layer for each system and segment, with uncollected sources marked as gaps

text.en: List the systems, segments and applications requiring detection coverage.
Name the log or telemetry source that would carry the evidence for each.
Record the control layer each source belongs to across the estate.
Mark every listed source not currently collected as an open gap.
Circulate the coverage list to the owners of the uncollected sources.

title.en: Define the alert threshold and escalation trigger for each anomaly type monitored

description.en: For every anomaly type in scope — including ICT network performance degradation, not only security events — record the condition that raises an alert, the value it fires at, who receives it, and the point at which it escalates into the incident process. Record thresholds as values rather than descriptions, so a later reviewer can tell whether one was changed and when. Attach the threshold register with an owner named per entry.

evidenceHint.en: Anomaly detection threshold register recording the firing value, the receiver and the escalation trigger for each anomaly type

text.en: List the anomaly types in scope, including network performance degradation.
Record the condition that raises an alert for each anomaly type listed.
Set the firing value as a number rather than a qualitative description.
Name the receiver of each alert and the trigger that escalates it.
Assign an owner to each threshold entry in the register.

title.en: Configure monitoring and alerting on every source in the detection coverage list

description.en: Turn the coverage list and the threshold register into deployed configuration: collection enabled on each source, a rule implementing each threshold, and each alert routed to the receiver named in the register. Export the configuration rather than describing it, so the export can be read against the register entry by entry. Attach the monitoring and alerting configuration export alongside the coverage rows it satisfies.

evidenceHint.en: Monitoring and alerting configuration export showing collection enabled per source and a rule per threshold, mapped to the coverage rows it satisfies

title.en: Publish the log review procedure naming who reviews which logs and what they record

description.en: Write the procedure a reviewer follows: which log sets are reviewed, by which role, what is looked for, what gets recorded when nothing is found, and how a suspected anomaly is handed into the incident process. A procedure that never says what a clean review looks like produces no evidence in the periods where nothing happened, which is most of them. Attach the approved log review procedure.

evidenceHint.en: Approved log review procedure naming the reviewer role, the log sets in scope and the record kept for a review that finds nothing

title.en: Log every alert raised in the period together with its triage outcome

description.en: Record each alert the monitoring raised during the period: the threshold that fired it, when it arrived, who triaged it, the conclusion reached, and whether it was escalated into the incident process. Entries closed as noise carry the reason they were closed. With the completed log reviews, this is the record showing detection actually ran rather than merely being configured. Attach the alert triage record and the period's completed log reviews.

evidenceHint.en: Alert triage record for the period showing each alert, the threshold that fired it, the reviewer, the outcome and any escalation, with the completed log reviews

title.en: Test each detection rule with a simulated anomalous event and record whether the alert fired

description.en: Exercise the detection mechanisms rather than inspecting their configuration: generate a controlled event that should breach each threshold in the register and record whether the alert fired, how long it took to arrive, and whether it reached the receiver named for it. Every rule that did not fire is a finding with an owner and a fix date. Attach the test results, one row per rule tested, including the rules that passed.

evidenceHint.en: Detection test results, one row per rule tested, recording the simulated event, whether the alert fired, the time to arrive and the receiver reached

text.en: Select the thresholds to be exercised and agree the simulated events.
Generate each controlled event in a way that does not disturb live service.
Record whether the alert fired and how long it took to arrive.
Confirm the alert reached the receiver named in the threshold register.
Raise a finding with an owner and fix date for every rule that stayed silent.

templates.title: Response and recovery / ICT business continuity
templates.description: Identify the critical functions ICT continuity must sustain and the services each depends on, estimate the impact of their disruption, and hold response and recovery plans written against those figures.
templates.objective: To ensure every critical business function has a recovery objective grounded in its estimated loss and a plan that testing has shown can reach it.
templates.successCriteria:
Each critical function names its business owner, the ICT and third-party services it depends on, and the outage it can absorb.
Recovery time and point objectives follow from a recorded impact and loss estimate whose assumptions are stated.
The continuity policy states who may activate it, the stand-down route, the test cycle and its review owner.
Each function's plan names its activation trigger, recovery sequence and restoration criteria, and was exercised within the test cycle.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the critical function register with owners, ICT and third-party dependencies and absorbable outage.
Request the impact and loss estimates with their assumptions and the recovery objectives agreed per function.
Collect the ICT business continuity policy with its activation authority, stand-down route and test cycle.
Obtain the response and recovery plans and the BCP test results and post-test reviews for the period.

Analysis:
Confirm each function rated critical elsewhere has a register entry whose dependencies reach third-party services, not internal systems alone.
Test whether the agreed recovery objectives sit consistently with the loss estimate and absorbable outage for the same function.
Check each plan names an activation trigger observable during an incident and a restoration criterion a responder could judge.
Compare the recovery time and point achieved in each test with that function's objectives and quantify the shortfall.
Verify steps recorded as not completed became amendments with owners and that the plan was re-issued.

Output:
Plan coverage schedule listing critical functions with no current response and recovery plan.
Objective-versus-achieved table for every plan exercised in the period.
Amendment tracker showing shortfalls closed, shortfalls open and the plan versions re-issued.

title.en: Record the critical functions ICT continuity must sustain and the ICT services each one depends on

description.en: Build the register the continuity policy and the recovery plans are both written against. One row per critical function, naming the business owner, the ICT systems, internal services and third-party services the function cannot run without, and the outage the function can absorb before the damage this control exists to limit begins. Source the dependency rows from the teams that actually run those services rather than from an org chart or a diagram, so the register reflects what carries the function today. Management confirms which functions are critical; IT Operations supplies the dependency detail. Attach the register, dated and version-marked.

evidenceHint.en: Critical function register: function, business owner, the ICT systems and third-party services it depends on, and the outage it can absorb

text.en: Name each function the business treats as critical and the owner accountable for it.
List the ICT systems, internal services and providers each function cannot run without.
Record the outage each function can absorb before the damage becomes material.
Have the service and provider owners confirm the dependency rows before issue.
Date and version-mark the register and pass it to whoever writes the plans.

title.en: Estimate the impact and losses a disruption of each critical function would cause and set its recovery objectives

description.en: For every row of the critical function register, estimate what a disruption costs — operational, financial and client impact — and how that cost grows with the length of the outage. Use those estimates to set a recovery time objective and a recovery point objective for the function, so the plans have a target that a test can be measured against rather than an aspiration. Record the assumptions each estimate rests on and who agreed them, so the figures can be challenged, re-used and revised when the function changes. Attach the impact estimate together with the recovery objectives it produced.

evidenceHint.en: Impact and loss estimate per critical function, stating the assumptions relied on and the recovery time and recovery point objective agreed

title.en: Issue the ICT business continuity policy stating who may activate it and what it commits the organisation to

description.en: Turn the register and the recovery objectives into the policy this control requires. State the scope — which critical functions and ICT services it covers — who holds the authority to declare a disruption and activate the plans, how activation is escalated and stood down, the recovery objectives the organisation commits to, the cycle on which the plans are tested, and how continuity work connects to incident handling so the two do not run separate accounts of the same event. Name the review owner, date and version the document, and record the approval it was issued under. Attach the approved policy.

evidenceHint.en: Approved and dated ICT business continuity policy carrying its version, scope, activation authority, stand-down route, plan test cycle and named review owner

title.en: Write a response and recovery plan for each critical function naming its activation trigger and recovery sequence

description.en: One plan per critical function in the register. Each states the trigger that activates it, the named responders and their deputies, the order in which the ICT services behind the function are recovered, the fallback available to the business while recovery runs, the third-party providers the sequence depends on and how they are reached outside working hours, and the condition under which the function is declared restored. Where a step relies on backup and restoration procedures, cite them rather than duplicating them, so only one version can drift. Attach the plan set with each plan's owner and version.

evidenceHint.en: Response and recovery plan per critical function: activation trigger, responder roles, recovery sequence, third-party contacts and the restoration criteria

text.en: Take the recovery time and recovery point objectives for the function from the impact estimate.
Order the ICT services behind the function into the sequence they must be recovered in.
Name a responder and a deputy against each step of that sequence.
Record how each third-party provider in the sequence is reached outside working hours.
State the condition under which the function is declared restored to the business.

title.en: Test each response and recovery plan at least annually and record what the test achieved against its objectives

description.en: Exercise the plans on the cycle the policy sets, and at least annually as this control requires. For each test record the scenario used, the plan and critical function exercised, who took part, the recovery time and recovery point actually achieved, every step that could not be completed and the reason it could not. A test that met its objective and a test that did not are both results, and both are filed — a plan only exercised successfully is a plan never stressed. Attach the test results for the period.

evidenceHint.en: BCP test results for the period: scenario, plan and function exercised, participants, recovery time and recovery point achieved, and every step not completed

title.en: Compare each recorded test result against the plan's recovery objectives and log the amendments the shortfalls require

description.en: After each test cycle, read the results against the recovery objectives set for the function and decide, for every gap, whether the plan, the objective or the underlying ICT capacity has to change. Record the decision, the owner and the date the amendment is due to land, then re-issue the affected plans under a new version number so the version that was tested stays identifiable. A gap carried forward without an amendment is recorded with the reason it was accepted, so acceptance is a decision somebody made rather than a silence. Attach the review record and the re-issued plans.

evidenceHint.en: Post-test review record: each recovery objective met or missed, the amendment decided for each miss, its owner, and the new version of every plan re-issued

text.en: List each recovery objective the test met and each one it missed.
Decide for every miss whether the plan, the objective or the ICT capacity changes.
Name the owner and the date each amendment is due to land.
Re-issue every amended plan under a new version number.
Record the reason for any gap accepted without an amendment.

templates.title: Backup, restoration and recovery procedures
templates.description: Record every system and data set in backup scope with its frequency and retention, decide which warrant redundant ICT capacity, and hold restoration procedures that have been exercised rather than assumed.
templates.objective: To ensure every system in backup scope can actually be restored at the frequency, retention and separation the policy fixes, rather than assumed from a job that runs.
templates.successCriteria:
Each system and data set in backup scope records an owner, a frequency, a retention period and the job producing the copy.
Copies are held with the separation from their source system that the policy requires, confirmed row by row.
Every in-scope system has a restoration procedure giving restore steps, dependency order and post-restore verification checks.
A restore has been performed on the policy's cycle for each system, and any system without a successful restore is owned and dated.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the backup scope register with owner, frequency, retention and producing job per system or data set.
Request the redundant capacity records stating whether redundancy is warranted, what stands behind each system and how it is switched to.
Collect the backup policy with its frequency and retention bands, separation requirement, restore authority and test cycle.
Obtain the restoration procedures, the recovery test logs for the period and the backup coverage reconciliation.

Analysis:
Compare job schedules in the backup platform with the frequency recorded in the register and list jobs running less often.
Confirm configured retention matches the policy bands and that copies sit apart from the system they protect.
Check each redundancy decision gives a reason and, where warranted, a switchover method that has been exercised.
Walk one restoration procedure through with its owner to test whether the steps and dependency order can be followed as written.
Reconcile the test logs with the register, count systems marked untested or failed, and read the deviations recorded.

Output:
Register-to-platform comparison showing frequency and retention mismatches by system.
Restore results table giving the copy used, elapsed time and verification outcome per system.
Untested and failed-restore list with an owner and remediation date against each row.

title.en: Record every system and data set in backup scope with the frequency and retention set for each

description.en: Build the backup scope register that the policy, the procedures and the restore tests all work from. One row per system or data set, naming its owner, the data it holds, the backup frequency, how long each copy is retained and the backup job or platform that produces it. Take the rows from the running backup configuration as well as from the systems inventory, so a system configured for no backup at all appears as a row with the gap recorded rather than as an absence nobody notices. System owners confirm the retention their data needs. Attach the register with its date and version.

evidenceHint.en: Backup scope register: system or data set, owner, backup frequency, retention period and the backup job that produces the copy

text.en: List every system and data set held in the systems inventory.
Read the configured frequency and retention out of the backup platform.
Have each system owner confirm the retention their data requires.
Record every in-scope system with no backup job as an open gap with an owner.

title.en: Record which in-scope systems warrant redundant ICT capacity and what capacity stands behind each

description.en: The framework asks for redundant ICT capacity where it is appropriate, so decide where that is and write the decision down rather than leaving it to inference. Against each row of the scope register, record whether redundant capacity is warranted, the reasoning behind that answer, and — where it is warranted — the capacity actually in place, where it runs, and how a switch to it is made and by whom. Systems judged not to warrant redundancy carry their reason too, so the judgement can be revisited when the system's role changes. Attach the redundant capacity record.

evidenceHint.en: Redundant capacity records: each in-scope system, whether redundancy is warranted and why, the capacity in place, where it runs and how it is switched to

title.en: Issue the backup policy fixing frequency, retention and the separation required between a copy and its source system

description.en: Write the policy this control names, drawing its parameters from the scope register rather than from a template. It states the backup frequency and retention bands and which systems fall into each, the requirement that copies be held securely and separately from the systems they were taken from, who may authorise and perform a restore, and the cycle on which restoration is tested. Where a system cannot meet a band, the policy records the exception and its owner instead of being silently untrue. Record the approval it was issued under, date and version it, and attach the approved policy.

evidenceHint.en: Approved and dated backup policy stating the frequency and retention bands, the storage separation required, restore authority, the test cycle and any recorded exceptions

title.en: Write the restoration and recovery procedure for each system in the backup scope register

description.en: One procedure per system, written so that somebody who did not build the system can follow it under pressure: where its copies are held, how a copy is selected for a particular point in time, the authorisation a restore requires before it starts, the restore steps in order, the dependent systems that must come back and in what sequence, and the checks that confirm the restored data is complete and usable. Name an owner and a version for each procedure so the one exercised in a test is identifiable afterwards. Attach the procedure set.

evidenceHint.en: Restoration procedures, one per in-scope system, each naming its owner, restore steps, dependency order and the post-restore verification checks

text.en: Record where the copies for the system are held and how a point in time is chosen.
Write the restore steps in the order they have to be run.
State the authorisation a restore requires before it begins.
List the dependent systems that must be recovered and in what order.
Define the checks that confirm the restored data is complete and usable.

title.en: Restore from backup on the cycle the policy sets and log the outcome for every system tested

description.en: Run the restoration tests the policy schedules, following the written procedure rather than the knowledge of whoever happens to run them — an untested procedure is the thing being tested. Log each test with the system, the backup copy restored and its date, who ran it, how long the restore took, whether the verification checks passed, and every deviation from the procedure that was needed to finish. Failed and partial restores are logged in the same place as successes, because they are the results that carry the most information. Attach the recovery test log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Recovery test logs for the period: system, backup copy restored, operator, elapsed time, verification result and any deviation from the written procedure

title.en: Reconcile the recovery test logs against the backup scope register and record every system with no successful restore

description.en: Match the test logs line by line to the scope register and produce the coverage view: every in-scope system marked tested and verified, tested and failed, or not tested in the cycle. In the same pass confirm that each tested system's copies still sit on storage separate from the system they came from, since a separation set once and never re-checked drifts back quietly. Record the cause, owner and remediation date against each failure and each miss, and remove the register rows for systems no longer in the estate. Attach the reconciliation.

evidenceHint.en: Backup coverage reconciliation: every register row marked tested, failed or untested, storage separation confirmed per row, and an owner and date against each gap

templates.title: Learning and evolving (post-incident review)
templates.description: Draw on named sources of vulnerability, incident and cyber-threat information, and run post-incident review to a published procedure so what an incident taught becomes a change to the framework.
templates.objective: To turn what incidents and threat intelligence reveal into named changes to the ICT risk framework and into the awareness staff actually receive.
templates.successCriteria:
Each vulnerability, incident and cyber-threat source records its category, delivery route, named reader and reading cadence.
Every major incident has a filed review report giving its timeline, contributing causes and actions with owners and dates.
Each lessons-learned entry names the framework element it changes, not only the incident it came from.
The awareness programme reached its audience, with completion recorded per participant and follow-up for those outstanding.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the intake records naming each intelligence source, its category, route, named reader and cadence.
Request the post-incident review procedure with the incidents in scope and the contents a report must carry.
Collect the lessons-learned register with the framework element, owner, due date and status per entry.
Obtain the review reports filed for the period, the awareness programme records and the closure review.

Analysis:
Compare major incidents logged in the period with the reports filed and identify those reviewed late or not at all.
Test whether each report separates contributing causes from the triggering event as the procedure requires.
Trace sampled register entries to the document, policy or procedure they name and confirm the change was made there.
Ask each named reader for the items last considered from their source and compare the interval with the recorded cadence.
Measure awareness completion against the intended audience and examine the follow-up taken for non-completions.

Output:
Incident-to-review coverage table giving the review interval per major incident.
Closure results separating entries closed by a traceable framework change from those still open, with their age.
Awareness completion rate by audience, naming the population still outstanding.

title.en: Record the sources of vulnerability, incident and cyber-threat information the framework draws on

description.en: List where information actually reaches the organisation from — vendor and product advisories, national or sector CERT feeds, threat-intelligence subscriptions, information-sharing arrangements, and the organisation's own incident and vulnerability findings — and for each record the feed, how it arrives, the named person who reads it and how often. Record any of the three categories this control names (vulnerabilities, ICT-related incidents, cyber threats) for which no source exists, so the gap is visible rather than presumed covered by the others. Attach the intake register, dated and version-marked.

evidenceHint.en: Threat-intelligence intake records: each source, the category it covers, its delivery route, the named reader and the cadence at which it is read

text.en: List every advisory, feed and sharing arrangement already being received.
Name the person who reads each source and how often they read it.
Map each source to the categories it covers: vulnerability, incident, threat.
Record every category with no source against it as an open intake gap.

title.en: Publish the post-incident review procedure setting which incidents it covers and what its report must record

description.en: Write the procedure that makes reviews happen without a fresh decision each time: which incidents trigger a review — major ICT-related incidents at minimum, as this control requires — the point after closure at which it is held, who must attend, what the report has to record (timeline, contributing causes, how detection and response performed, and the actions arising with owners), and where reports are filed so they can be found later. Name the procedure owner and version it. Attach the published procedure.

evidenceHint.en: Published post-incident review procedure naming the incidents in scope, the attendees required, the contents of the report and where reports are filed

title.en: Open a lessons-learned register that routes each finding to the framework element it changes

description.en: Stand up the register the control's feedback loop runs on. One row per lesson, carrying its source (post-incident review, threat notification, test or audit finding), the lesson itself, the element of the ICT risk management framework it changes — policy, plan, control, training or tooling — the named owner, the due date and the current status. A lesson with no framework element named against it is not filed until it has one, because that link is the whole point of the register rather than a field on it. Attach the register with its structure and current contents.

evidenceHint.en: Lessons-learned register: the source of each lesson, the framework element it changes, the named owner, the due date and the current status

title.en: Hold a post-incident review for each major incident and file its report

description.en: Run the review the procedure requires for every major ICT-related incident closed in the period, with the attendees it names. Produce a report carrying the incident timeline, the contributing causes, an assessment of how detection and response actually performed, and the actions arising with an owner and date against each. Open the corresponding lessons-learned rows during the same session, so nothing depends on somebody remembering afterwards. Where a major incident was closed without a review, record that and the reason. Attach the reports for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Post-incident review reports for the period, each carrying the timeline, contributing causes, the response assessment and the actions raised with owners and dates

title.en: Deliver the ICT security awareness and training programme and record who completed it

description.en: Run the awareness and training the framework commits to for this period and evidence delivery rather than intent: what was delivered, to which audience, the content covered, the dates, the completion record per person or team, and the follow-up for anyone outstanding. Where recent incidents or threat notifications changed the material, note which ones, so the programme visibly moves with what the organisation has learned instead of repeating last year's deck. HR supplies the audience list and chases completion; Security engineering owns the content.

evidenceHint.en: Awareness programme records for the period: material delivered, audience, dates, completion per participant and the follow-up for those outstanding

title.en: Check every lessons-learned entry reached the framework element it named and record those still open

description.en: Work through the register at the end of the cycle and verify each closed row against the change it claims: the amended policy version, the updated plan, the new or changed control, the revised training module. A row marked closed with no traceable change is reopened, since a closed row is the only evidence this control's feedback loop produces. For rows still open, record the age, the owner and whether the due date has moved, and escalate the ones carried across more than one cycle. Attach the review with its links to the changes it verified.

evidenceHint.en: Lessons-learned closure review: every entry with the framework change that closed it, or its age, owner and the reason it remains open

text.en: List the register rows marked closed since the previous review.
Locate the amended policy, plan, control or training module behind each one.
Reopen any row whose claimed change cannot be located.
Record the age and the owner of every row still open.
Escalate the rows carried across more than one review cycle.

templates.title: Crisis communication
templates.description: Name the audiences a major ICT incident must reach and the channel held for each, and hold a crisis communication plan that states who may activate it.
templates.objective: To ensure every audience owed information in a major ICT incident is reached over a held channel by a named spokesperson with a message someone authorised.
templates.successCriteria:
Each audience on the communication map states why it is in scope, the channel that reaches it and who holds its contact list.
The crisis plan sets its activation trigger, the order audiences are addressed, the approval path and the holding statement.
Every audience has a named spokesperson and deputy with their speaking authority recorded.
Messages issued in an incident are logged with audience, channel, release time, approver and the version actually sent.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the stakeholder communication map with each audience, its channel, contact-list holder and any commitment made.
Request the crisis communication plan with its activation trigger, audience sequence, approval path and holding statement.
Collect the spokesperson records naming spokesperson, deputy, contact routes and authority to speak unaided.
Obtain the internal and external notification procedures, the crisis communications log and the review record.

Analysis:
Check the audience list against regulatory notification duties, contractual commitments and clients affected by past incidents.
Test sampled contact routes for reachability and compare the last verification date with the plan's refresh cycle.
Confirm the notification procedures name a drafter, the facts to confirm, an approver and a channel for each route.
Compare logged messages with the plan's audience sequence, noting releases made without the approval recorded.

Output:
Audience coverage table naming audiences with no held channel or no contact-list holder.
Spokesperson schedule showing vacancies, missing deputies and unverified contact routes.
Communications conformance findings for the period's incidents, with unapproved releases listed.

title.en: Record the audiences a major ICT incident must be communicated to and the channel held for each

description.en: Map the audiences this control names — clients, counterparts and the public — alongside the internal audiences a crisis needs reached: staff, the management body, the service teams. For each, record what puts them in scope for a given incident, the channel that actually reaches them (status page, account manager, email, press contact), who holds the contact list and where it lives, and any contractual or arrangement-based commitment already made about informing them. Legal/DPO confirms the commitments that create a duty to inform. Attach the map, dated and version-marked.

evidenceHint.en: Stakeholder communication map: audience, what puts them in scope, the channel that reaches them, the contact-list holder and any commitment already made

title.en: Issue the crisis communication plan naming its activation trigger, approval path and first-message content

description.en: Write the plan this control requires: the trigger that puts it into effect, who decides that a major ICT-related incident warrants external communication, the sequence in which the mapped audiences are addressed, the approval a message needs before release, the holding-statement content used while facts are still being established, and the point at which the plan itself is next reviewed. Set out how the plan draws on the incident record so communications and incident handling do not maintain two versions of the same event. Record the approval it was issued under, date and version it, and attach the plan.

evidenceHint.en: Approved and dated crisis communication plan carrying its activation trigger, audience sequence, approval path and holding-statement content

title.en: Name the spokesperson and deputy for each audience and record where their contact details are held

description.en: Assign the communication roles this control asks to be designated, and record them somewhere a responder can reach at three in the morning: for each audience on the map, the named spokesperson, their deputy, the contact routes for both, and the authority each holds to speak without further approval.
