Include the person who approves external statements and the person who keeps this record current. Confirm each name with the individual concerned, so no role is held by somebody unaware they hold it. Attach the designated spokesperson record.

evidenceHint.en: Designated spokesperson records: audience, named spokesperson and deputy, their contact routes, and the authority each holds to speak unaided

title.en: Write the internal and external disclosure procedures covering who drafts, who approves and who releases

description.en: Turn the plan into the step-by-step procedures this control names — one for internal notification, one for external disclosure. Each states what triggers a notification, who drafts it, which facts must be confirmed before release and by whom, who approves it, the channel used, and the record kept of what was sent and when. Where an audience carries a commitment recorded in the communication map, the procedure follows that commitment rather than restating a general rule over the top of it. Legal/DPO owns the wording; Management approves. Attach both procedures with owner and version.

evidenceHint.en: Stakeholder notification procedures, internal and external, each naming the trigger, the drafter, the facts to confirm, the approver, the channel and the record kept

text.en: State what triggers a notification to each audience on the map.
Name who drafts, who confirms the facts and who approves before release.
Record the channel used for each audience and the fallback if it is unavailable.
Define what is recorded about every message sent and where that record lives.
Reference the commitments in the communication map rather than restating them.

title.en: Record every communication issued during a major incident with the audience, channel and approver

description.en: Keep one running log across incidents so what was said, to whom, and when can be reconstructed afterwards without reassembling inboxes. Each entry carries the incident reference, the audience, the channel, the time the message was released, who drafted it and who approved it, and the message text or a link to the exact version issued. Corrections and follow-ups are logged against the original entry rather than as new events, so a reader can follow one story. This log is the artifact attached for the evidence period.

evidenceHint.en: Crisis communications log for the period: incident, audience, channel, release time, drafter, approver and the message version actually issued

title.en: Review the communications issued against the plan and refresh the contact and spokesperson records

description.en: After each incident that triggered external communication — and at the plan's review point where none occurred — compare what was issued with what the plan and procedures said would be issued: audiences reached and missed, approvals obtained, and timing against the sequence set. Record each divergence with the amendment it requires and the owner of that amendment. In the same pass re-verify the contact routes and spokesperson names, correct what has changed, and note the date checked so staleness is measurable. Attach the review.

evidenceHint.en: Communication review record: each divergence from the plan with its amendment and owner, plus the re-verified contact and spokesperson entries with the date checked

templates.title: Simplified ICT risk management framework
templates.description: Determine eligibility for the simplified regime against each criterion it turns on, and record the proportionality assessment linking the framework actually operated to that determination.
templates.objective: To ensure reliance on the simplified regime rests on a recorded eligibility determination and a proportionality judgement revisited as the entity's profile changes.
templates.successCriteria:
The eligibility determination covers every criterion the regime turns on, with the entity's figures and the date recorded.
The proportionality assessment states the depth chosen for each framework element and the reasoning for what is left out.
The simplified framework names the critical functions it protects, the measures in place and an owner per part.
Each cycle records the ICT risk position and its movement, the period's incidents and every critical function's continuity status.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the eligibility determination with the entity's position and figures against each criterion of the regime.
Request the proportionality assessment with the risk profile, the depth chosen per element and the reasoning for omissions.
Collect the simplified ICT risk framework document with its critical functions, measures and named owners.
Obtain the monitoring records for each cycle and the latest re-verification of eligibility and proportionality.

Analysis:
Recalculate each eligibility criterion from the entity's own financial and staffing records and compare with the determination.
Test whether elements omitted under proportionality are reasoned from the risk profile rather than from resource constraints.
Compare the critical functions named in the framework with those the business identifies as critical elsewhere.
Check a monitoring record exists for every cycle and shows movement rather than a position repeated unchanged.
Confirm the re-verification used current figures and concluded on whether the regime still applies.

Output:
Eligibility recalculation showing the determined and recalculated position per criterion.
Proportionality findings listing elements omitted without a risk-based reason.
Monitoring completeness record with the continuity status reported for each critical function.

title.en: Record the eligibility determination for the simplified regime against each criterion it turns on

description.en: Establish in writing whether this entity is one of those the simplified framework is available to, rather than assuming it from size. Take each criterion the regime turns on, record the entity's position against it with the figures or facts relied on and where those came from, and state the resulting determination and its date. Where a criterion sits close to its boundary, record that and when the position will next be checked, because that is the one most likely to move without anybody noticing. Legal/DPO makes the determination on the evidence and records who accepted it and on what date. Attach the determination with its supporting figures.

evidenceHint.en: Eligibility determination for the simplified regime: each criterion, the entity's position with the figures relied on, the conclusion reached, and the date it was recorded

title.en: Write the proportionality assessment linking each part of the framework to the entity's risk profile

description.en: Set out the entity's ICT risk profile — its size, the nature and complexity of the ICT services it runs, its interconnections, and the critical functions it carries — and then, against each part of the ICT risk framework it will operate, record what it does, why that depth is proportionate to the profile, and what was deliberately not done and on what reasoning. This assessment is what makes a simplified framework defensible rather than merely smaller, so the omissions are the part worth writing carefully. Attach it with its date and its author.

evidenceHint.en: Proportionality assessment: the entity's risk profile, each framework element with the depth chosen for it, and the reasoning for everything left out

title.en: Document the simplified ICT risk management framework and the critical functions it protects

description.en: Produce the framework document itself, at the depth the proportionality assessment justifies: the critical functions it protects, how ICT risks are identified, rated and recorded, the protective measures in place, how ICT-related incidents are handled, how continuity of those critical functions is provided for, and who owns each part. Cross-reference the proportionality assessment at each choice of depth so a reader sees the reasoning without needing a second document beside it. Record the date, the version and the approval it was issued under, and attach the framework document.

evidenceHint.en: Approved and dated simplified ICT risk framework document naming the critical functions covered, the measures in place and the owner of each part

text.en: List the critical functions the framework is written to protect.
Record how ICT risks are identified, rated and kept up to date.
Describe the protective measures standing behind each critical function.
State how continuity of each critical function is provided for.
Name the owner of each part and the point at which the document is reviewed.

title.en: Record the ICT risk position and the continuity status of each critical function each cycle

description.en: Run the monitoring the framework commits to and leave a record rather than a conversation. Each cycle, capture the open ICT risks and how they have moved since the last one, the incidents and disruptions that occurred in the period, the status of the measures protecting each critical function, and whether the continuity arrangements for those functions were exercised or actually invoked. Note anything that has shifted the entity's risk profile, since that is what feeds the eligibility and proportionality re-check rather than waiting to be rediscovered there. Attach the monitoring record for the period.

evidenceHint.en: ICT risk and continuity monitoring record for the period: open risks and their movement, incidents in the period, and the continuity status of each critical function

title.en: Re-verify the eligibility determination and proportionality assessment against the entity's current profile

description.en: At the review point the framework document sets, take the determination and the assessment back to the current facts: the figures behind each eligibility criterion, the ICT services and interconnections now in place, and the critical functions now carried. Record whether the simplified regime still applies and whether each proportionality judgement still holds; where either has moved, name the change required, its owner and the date it is due. A re-verification that finds nothing changed is recorded too, with the figures it was checked against, so the check is distinguishable from a check nobody ran. Attach the re-verification.

evidenceHint.en: Re-verification record: the current figures for each eligibility criterion, whether the regime still applies, and each proportionality judgement confirmed or changed

templates.title: ICT-related incident management process
templates.description: Define what counts as an ICT-related incident and the detection sources that raise one, and document the management procedure that carries it from detection to closure.
templates.objective: To ensure an event recognised as an ICT-related incident enters a defined process, reaches the people named to handle it, and closes on a recorded resolution.
templates.successCriteria:
The detection-source list states, per source, what it reports, who receives it and how it enters the incident process.
The issued procedure is versioned and covers detection, registration, handling, logging and resolution with no stage unowned.
Every incident-handling role has a named holder and deputy who confirmed the assignment, with a contact route recorded.
Each logged incident shows its detection source, handling times, handler, escalations sent and how it was resolved.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the incident scope definition and detection-source list with each source's recipient and entry route.
Request the issued ICT-related incident management procedure with its version and date.
Collect the role assignment table with holders, deputies, contact routes and confirmation dates.
Obtain the early-warning procedure with its templates and trigger-to-recipient list, and the incident log for the period.

Analysis:
Compare the listed detection sources with the monitoring and service-desk channels in use and find any entering no route.
Walk one closed incident end to end against the procedure and note stages performed outside it or left unrecorded.
Confirm named holders and deputies were in post throughout the period and that each assignment was confirmed.
Check incidents meeting an early-warning trigger produced the notification to the recipient listed against it.
Read the conformance check for incidents marked partial or missed and test whether a cause and correction were recorded.

Output:
Detection-source routing table naming sources whose output reaches no incident route.
Role coverage schedule listing unconfirmed, vacant or deputy-less incident-handling roles.
Escalation conformance results with each deviation and the correction recorded against it.

title.en: Define what counts as an ICT-related incident and list the detection sources that raise one

description.en: Write down the criteria that make an event an ICT-related incident for this entity, so the process has a decidable entry point, and list every source that can raise one — monitoring and alerting tools, service desk tickets, staff reports, and notifications from ICT third-party providers. For each source record what it sends, who receives it, and how that report reaches the incident process. Attach the completed definition and source list; it is the scope that the incident procedure, the incident log and the escalation path are all built against.

evidenceHint.en: Incident scope definition with the detection-source list: each source, what it reports, its recipient and the route into the incident process

text.en: State the criteria that separate an ICT-related incident from a routine service event.
List every detection and reporting source that can raise an incident, with its owner.
Record how each source's report reaches the incident process and who receives it.
Name any source that cannot currently reach the process, so the gap is visible.

title.en: Document the ICT-related incident management procedure from detection to resolution

description.en: Produce the incident management procedure an auditor asks for. It has to carry the whole path an incident travels: how it is detected and registered, who triages it, how it is handled and contained, how progress is recorded, what closes it, and what is written into the incident log at each of those points. Reference the detection sources from the scope task so every intake route lands in the same procedure rather than a side channel. Attach the issued procedure with its version number and issue date.

evidenceHint.en: The issued ICT-related incident management procedure, versioned and dated, covering detection, registration, handling, logging and resolution

text.en: Describe intake and registration for each detection source in the scope list.
Set out triage, handling, containment and resolution with the role performing each.
State what is recorded in the incident log at registration, during handling and at closure.
Define the conditions under which an incident is closed and who confirms them.
Issue the procedure with a version number and record where it is published.

title.en: Record the named holder and deputy for every incident-handling role the procedure defines

description.en: The procedure names roles; this task names people. Build a table with one row per role the incident procedure relies on — the coordinator, the technical responders, communications, and whoever decides escalation — giving the current holder, a deputy covering absence, and the contact route for each. Confirm with each named person that they know they hold the role, since an unstaffed role is indistinguishable from a staffed one on paper. Attach the table with the date it was last confirmed.

evidenceHint.en: Incident-handling role assignment table: role, named holder, deputy, contact route and the date each holder confirmed the assignment

title.en: Establish the early-warning and internal notification path for ICT-related incidents

description.en: Write the early-warning and escalation procedure that sits beside the incident procedure: the conditions that raise an early warning, who is notified when each escalation trigger is met, through which channel, and what the notification has to contain for the recipient to act on it. Cover internal notification to the roles in the assignment table, and record the fallback route used when a named recipient cannot be reached. Attach the escalation procedure together with the notification templates it refers to.

evidenceHint.en: The early-warning and escalation procedure with its notification templates and the trigger-to-recipient list

text.en: List the escalation triggers the incident procedure recognises and the condition for each.
Name the recipients notified at each trigger and the channel used to reach them.
State what an early-warning notification must contain so the recipient can act on it.
Record the fallback route to use when a named recipient cannot be reached.

title.en: Log every ICT-related incident with its handling timeline and how it was resolved

description.en: Keep the incident log as the single record of every ICT-related incident registered in the period. Each entry carries the identifier, the detection source and time of detection, what was affected, the roles that handled it, the escalations and notifications actually sent with their times, the actions taken, and the resolution with the time of closure. An incident that was raised and then dismissed is logged too, with the reason for dismissal. The log export for the period is the artifact attached as evidence.

evidenceHint.en: Incident log export for the period: one row per ICT-related incident with detection source, times, handler, escalations sent, actions taken and resolution

title.en: Verify that the incidents closed in the period followed the escalation and notification path

description.en: Take the closed incidents from the log and check each against the escalation procedure: for every trigger an incident met, was the notification it requires sent, to the recipients named, and recorded. Mark each incident as followed, partially followed or missed, and for every deviation record the cause — a recipient nobody could reach, a trigger the procedure does not cover, a notification sent but never logged — and the correction it calls for. Attach the completed check with its findings.

evidenceHint.en: Escalation conformance check for the period: each closed incident marked followed, partial or missed, with the cause and correction for every deviation

text.en: List the incidents closed in the period from the incident log export.
Compare each incident's recorded notifications against the triggers it met.
Mark every deviation found and record the cause behind it.
Assign an owner to each correction the deviations call for.

templates.title: Incident classification
templates.description: Hold the DORA classification criteria and the data each one needs as a matrix, and record the materiality thresholds that turn an ICT-related incident into a major one.
templates.objective: To ensure each ICT-related incident is measured against the classification criteria and declared major or not by a named decider working from recorded figures.
templates.successCriteria:
Each classification criterion carries a measurement, a unit, a data source and the role supplying it in an incident.
Materiality thresholds are recorded per criterion, citing the provision taken or the entity's own value with its reasoning.
The workflow holds a major-incident determination step with its inputs, a named deciding role and a record kept either way.
Classification records show the value measured per criterion and the decider, and reported cyber threats carry a significance assessment.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the classification matrix with the measurement, unit, data source and supplying role per criterion.
Request the materiality thresholds document with the provision cited or the reasoning for each entity-set value.
Collect the workflow section showing the major-incident determination step, its inputs and deciding role.
Obtain the classification decision records, the cyber threat significance assessments and the validation record.

Analysis:
Trace one criterion to the system holding its figure and test whether it could supply the measurement while an incident is live.
Compare each recorded threshold with the provision cited, and check entity-set values carry reasoning rather than a bare number.
Re-apply the matrix to sampled incidents and compare the result reached with the classification recorded at the time.
Identify incidents classified with no measured value against a criterion, and those where the decider is unnamed.
Review the threat significance assessments for conclusions that produced no recorded follow-up decision.

Output:
Findings on whether each criterion's data source can supply its measurement during a live incident.
Re-classification sampling results showing agreement and disagreement per incident examined.
Record of corrections raised against the classification matrix or the materiality thresholds.

title.en: Record the DORA classification criteria and the data each one needs in a classification matrix

description.en: Build the classification matrix as one row per criterion the classification rules set — clients affected, duration, geographical spread, data losses, criticality, and economic impact. For each row record what has to be measured, the unit it is expressed in, the system or team that supplies the measurement during an incident, and who produces it. Transcribe the criteria from DORA and the related RTS rather than paraphrasing them into new ones. Attach the completed matrix.

evidenceHint.en: Incident classification matrix: one row per criterion with the measurement required, its unit, its data source and the role that supplies it during an incident

text.en: Transcribe each classification criterion from DORA and the related RTS into its own row.
State the measurement each criterion needs and the unit it is expressed in.
Name the system or team that supplies that measurement during a live incident.
Record any criterion with no data source today, so the shortfall is visible.

title.en: Record the materiality thresholds that make an ICT-related incident major, citing their source

description.en: For each criterion in the matrix, record the threshold at which an incident becomes major, taking the value from DORA and its related RTS and citing beside it the provision it comes from. Where the rules leave a value for the entity to set, record the value chosen and the reasoning; where no threshold applies to a criterion, say so rather than leaving the row blank. A number with no cited source does not belong in this document. Attach it with its version and the date it was last checked against the rules.

evidenceHint.en: Materiality thresholds document: the threshold per classification criterion with the provision it is taken from, or the entity's chosen value and its reasoning, versioned and dated

title.en: Add the major-incident determination step to the incident workflow with a named decision-maker

description.en: Change the incident workflow so that deciding whether an incident is major is an explicit step with an owner rather than something inferred later from the record. Record where in the handling of an incident the determination is made, who makes it and who deputises, what has to be in front of them when they make it (the matrix measurements and the thresholds document), and what is written down when the answer is yes and when it is no. Attach the amended workflow or procedure section showing that step.

evidenceHint.en: The amended incident workflow section showing the major-incident determination step, its required inputs, the named decision-making role and what is recorded either way

title.en: Classify each ICT-related incident against the matrix and record the decision with its measurements

description.en: For every incident registered in the period, record the measured value for each criterion in the matrix, how it compared against the threshold, the resulting classification, whether the incident was determined major, who decided and when. An incident found not to be major is recorded in the same detail as one that is — the record of the decision is what makes it reviewable later. The classification records for the period are the artifact attached.

evidenceHint.en: Classification decision records for the period: per incident the measured value against each criterion, the resulting classification, the major determination, the decider and the date

title.en: Assess the significance of each cyber threat reported in the period and record the outcome

description.en: Cyber threats are assessed for significance rather than classified as incidents, so keep them in their own record. For each threat that reaches the team, record where it came from, what it targets, the assessment made against the significance criteria in use, the conclusion reached, and what follows from it. Where a threat is assessed as significant, note the decision taken on it so the record connects to any notification made about it. Attach the threat assessment record for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Cyber threat significance assessments for the period: source, target, assessment, conclusion and the follow-up decision recorded for each threat

title.en: Validate a sample of the period's classification decisions against the recorded thresholds

description.en: Take a sample of the period's classification records — including every incident determined major and a selection of those determined not major — and re-apply the matrix and the thresholds document that were in force at the time of each. Record whether each classification stands, and where it does not, name the criterion at fault and whether the cause was a missing measurement, a misread threshold or a matrix row with no usable data source. Attach the validation with its findings and the corrections raised.

evidenceHint.en: Classification validation record: the sample taken, the re-applied result per incident, the discrepancies found and the corrections raised against the matrix or thresholds

text.en: Select the sample, including every incident determined to be major in the period.
Re-apply the matrix and thresholds that were in force at the time of each incident.
Record whether each classification stands and name the criterion at fault where it does not.
Raise a correction for every matrix row or threshold the sample shows to be unusable.

templates.title: Major-incident reporting to competent authority
templates.description: Know the competent authority, its reporting channel and its templates, and hold a regulatory reporting procedure that meets each deadline the Regulation sets.
templates.objective: To ensure every major ICT-related incident reaches the entity's competent authority on the prescribed template, through the right channel and inside each reporting deadline.
templates.successCriteria:
The competent authority, its channel and the credential holder and deputy are recorded and current.
Each report stage carries a tracked due date computed from a cited counting event.
Every major incident in the period has all three reports submitted on the harmonised templates, with proof of submission.
Each significant cyber threat carries a notify-or-not decision with its reasoning and its decision-maker.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the reporting requirements record naming the competent authority, its submission channel, and the credential holder and deputy.
Collect the issued regulatory reporting procedure covering the initial, intermediate and final report stages.
Export the reporting deadline tracker configuration showing the counting event and cited provision behind each stage.
Retrieve the submitted reports for every major incident in the period with the acknowledgement or authority reference held against each.
Gather the voluntary threat-notification decision records for the period.

Analysis:
Confirm the harmonised templates on file are those the named authority currently requires, and that the credential holder and deputy are still in post.
Recompute each stage's due date from its counting event and compare it with the timestamp on the proof of submission.
Trace every incident classified major in the period into the reconciliation and confirm no stage is left unaccounted for.
Examine each significant cyber threat for a stated reasoning and an identified decision-maker, whether or not a notification followed.
Read the cause and correction recorded against every stage marked late or outstanding.

Output:
A schedule of major incidents marking each report stage on time, late or outstanding against its recomputed deadline.
A findings note on the currency of the authority record, its channel and its templates.
A summary of voluntary threat notifications made and of the decisions not to notify.

title.en: Record the competent authority for the entity and the reporting channel and templates it requires

description.en: Establish where a major-incident report actually goes before one is needed. Record the relevant competent authority, the submission channel it uses, who holds the credentials or account for that channel and who deputises, any registration the channel requires in advance, and the harmonised templates it expects for the initial, intermediate and final stages. Attach the record with the blank templates obtained, so the reporting path is provable without waiting for a live incident to test it.

evidenceHint.en: Reporting requirements record naming the competent authority, the submission channel, the credential holder and deputy, with the harmonised initial, intermediate and final templates attached

text.en: Name the competent authority the entity reports major ICT-related incidents to.
Record the submission channel and who holds access to it, including a deputy.
Obtain the harmonised initial, intermediate and final report templates in use.
Record any registration or onboarding the channel requires before a first submission.

title.en: Document the regulatory reporting procedure for the initial, intermediate and final reports

description.en: Write the procedure that turns a major-incident determination into three submitted reports. It states who prepares each report and from which source records, who reviews and approves it before it leaves, who submits it through the recorded channel, what is retained as proof of submission, and how a report is corrected or supplemented once it has been sent. Attach the issued procedure with its version number and issue date.

evidenceHint.en: The issued regulatory reporting procedure for major ICT-related incidents, naming the preparer, approver, submitter and retention point for each of the three report stages

title.en: Configure the reporting deadline tracker to open a due date for each report stage

description.en: Set the tracker up so a major-incident determination opens the initial, intermediate and final entries for that incident automatically. Enter the deadline the applicable RTS and ITS set for each stage and the event that deadline is counted from, taking both from the rules and citing the provision beside each — an assumed period must not be entered. Configure the tracker so the outstanding stage and its owner are visible for every open incident. Attach the configuration and one worked entry.

evidenceHint.en: Reporting deadline tracker configuration showing the three report stages, the deadline and counting event recorded for each with its cited provision, and the owner field

text.en: Create the three report-stage entries that open on a major-incident determination.
Enter each stage's deadline and counting event, citing the provision it comes from.
Set the owner field and the outstanding-stage view used to chase open reports.
Walk one past incident through the tracker to confirm the entries open as intended.

title.en: Issue the initial notification, intermediate report and final report for every major incident

description.en: For each incident determined major, prepare each report on the harmonised template, have it approved as the procedure requires, submit it through the recorded channel, and keep whatever proof of submission the channel yields — the acknowledgement, receipt or reference the authority returns where one is given, and the channel's own submission record where it is not. File the submitted copy alongside that proof against the incident record, and enter the submission time on the tracker entry. The submitted reports with the proof of submission filed against each are the evidence for the period.

evidenceHint.en: For each major incident: the submitted initial, intermediate and final reports on the harmonised templates, each with the proof of submission kept for it, being the authority's acknowledgement or reference where one was returned

title.en: Determine for each significant cyber threat whether to notify the authority, and record the decision

description.en: Notifying a significant cyber threat is voluntary, so what has to exist afterwards is the decision, not necessarily a notification. For each threat assessed as significant, record who considered notifying the competent authority, the reasoning, the decision reached, and — where the decision was to notify — the submission made and its acknowledgement. A decision not to notify is recorded in the same detail as a decision to notify. Attach the decision record for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Voluntary threat-notification decision record for the period: threat, decision-maker, reasoning, decision, and the submission and acknowledgement where one was made

title.en: Verify that every major incident in the period produced each report within its tracked deadline

description.en: Take the tracker entries for the period and check each against the filed submissions: was every stage submitted, was each within the deadline recorded for it, and is the proof of submission on file. Mark each stage as submitted on time, submitted late, or outstanding, and for every late or outstanding stage record the cause and the correction — a determination made too late for the clock, an owner who never saw the entry, a channel that rejected the submission. Attach the reconciliation with the tracker export it was made from.

evidenceHint.en: Reporting reconciliation for the period: each major incident's three stages marked on time, late or outstanding, with the cause and correction for every exception, over the tracker export

templates.title: Payment-related operational/security incident handling
templates.description: Determine whether the payment-related incident provisions apply to the entity and record the assessment, extending incident handling to operational and security payment incidents where they do.
templates.objective: To ensure operational and security payment-related incidents are brought inside ICT incident handling wherever the payment provisions apply to the entity.
templates.successCriteria:
A dated assessment records the entity's regulatory status and the payment services it places in scope.
Intake flags incidents against those in-scope services and notifies the owners the procedure names.
Payment incidents are logged with the service affected, how it was recognised and the classification reached.
Payment-flagged incidents follow the same classification and reporting path as any other ICT incident.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the scope-applicability assessment together with the authorisation evidencing the entity's regulatory status.
Collect the versioned payment-incident handling procedure showing the intake flag and the owners it notifies.
Export the incident log filtered to payment-related incidents for the period.
Retrieve the payment-incident conformance check covering the same period.

Analysis:
Compare the payment services named in scope against the services the entity's authorisation actually permits it to provide.
Read the procedure for the point at which the payment flag is set, and confirm classification and reporting continue unchanged from there.
Sample logged payment incidents for the service affected, the recognition route and a recorded classification decision.
Search the wider incident log for incidents that touched an in-scope payment service yet carry no payment flag.
Check that every step marked deficient in the conformance check has a cause and a correction against it.

Output:
A statement of the applicability conclusion and the payment services and systems it brings into scope.
A conformance table marking each payment-flagged incident complete or deficient.
A list of incidents flagged wrongly or never flagged, with the correction proposed for each.

title.en: Determine whether the payment-related incident provisions apply to the entity and record the assessment

description.en: Record the scope-applicability assessment: the entity's regulatory status — credit institution, payment institution, account information service provider, electronic money institution, or none of these — the authorisation or registration evidencing it, the conclusion on whether the payment-related incident provisions apply, and who reached that conclusion. Where they apply, list the payment services in scope and the ICT systems supporting each, since that list is what the incident procedure has to recognise. Attach the assessment with its date.

evidenceHint.en: Scope-applicability assessment: regulatory status with its evidencing authorisation, the applicability conclusion, the payment services and supporting systems in scope, the assessor and the date

text.en: State the entity's regulatory status and the authorisation or registration evidencing it.
Record the conclusion on whether the payment-related incident provisions apply.
List the payment services in scope and the ICT systems supporting each of them.
Name the person who made the determination and the date it was made.

title.en: Extend the incident handling procedure to operational and security payment-related incidents

description.en: Amend the incident management and reporting procedure so that operational and security payment-related incidents travel the same path as other ICT-related incidents rather than a parallel one that drifts. Record how such an incident is recognised and flagged at intake against the payment services in the applicability assessment, which payment-service owners are notified, and how the classification and reporting steps apply to it. Where payment operations genuinely need a step the general procedure lacks, add it and say why. Attach the amended procedure with its version and issue date.

evidenceHint.en: The payment-incident handling procedure, versioned and dated, showing intake flagging against the in-scope payment services, the owners notified, and how classification and reporting apply

title.en: Log each operational or security payment-related incident under the payment-incident procedure

description.en: Register every operational or security payment-related incident in the incident log with its payment flag set, recording the payment service affected, how the incident was recognised as payment-related, the classification decision reached and whether it was reported. The log export for the period filtered to those entries is the artifact attached, and it is what shows the provisions are being applied to real events rather than merely adopted on paper.

evidenceHint.en: Incident log export filtered to payment-related incidents for the period, showing the payment service affected, how it was recognised, the classification decision and the reporting outcome

title.en: Verify that the period's payment-related incidents were classified and reported like other ICT incidents

description.en: Take the payment-flagged entries from the log and check each carries the same artefacts any other ICT-related incident of that classification would: a classification record, a major determination, and where major, the report submissions with their acknowledgements. Record every entry where a step is missing, with its cause and the correction. Where an incident was flagged as payment-related in error, or should have been flagged and was not, record that too — the flag is what routes the provisions, so a wrong flag is the failure, not a clerical detail. Attach the completed check.

evidenceHint.en: Payment-incident conformance check for the period: each payment-flagged incident marked complete or deficient, with the missing step, cause and correction, plus any incident flagged wrongly or not at all

templates.title: Digital operational resilience testing programme
templates.description: Record which ICT systems the testing programme covers and the risk rating that sets each one's test priority, and document the programme that follows from it.
templates.objective: To ensure resilience testing is aimed by risk across the entity's ICT systems, performed by an independent party, and carried through to the remediation of what it finds.
templates.successCriteria:
Every system in the testing scope register carries a risk rating and the test priority that follows from it.
The programme names its test types, how priority is set and its place in the ICT risk management framework.
Each in-scope system holds a test type, a test window and a named performing party.
No engagement began before its signed independence confirmation was accepted.
Findings run from prioritisation to the verification that closed them.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the testing scope register with each system's critical marking, risk rating and resulting test priority.
Collect the versioned resilience testing programme and the ICT risk management framework it points to.
Retrieve the test plan and schedule with its coverage view across the programme cycle.
Gather the signed tester independence confirmations accepted for the tests performed in the period.
Export the remediation tracker for findings raised in the period.

Analysis:
Judge whether the reasoning behind each risk rating supports the test priority assigned, and that every excluded system states why.
Trace the programme's prioritisation rule into the schedule and confirm the highest-priority systems hold the earlier windows.
Compare the date each independence confirmation was accepted with the start date of the engagement it covers.
Follow a sample of findings from the test report into the tracker and on to the verification recorded at closure.
Read the coverage review for critical systems marked not reached and confirm each carries a cause and a plan change.

Output:
A programme-cycle coverage statement marking each critical system tested, scheduled or not reached.
A note on any engagement that began before its independence confirmation was accepted.
An ageing list of findings still open past their agreed remediation date.

title.en: Record the ICT systems the testing programme covers and the risk rating that sets their test priority

description.en: The programme is risk-based, so it needs a rated population before it needs a schedule. List the ICT systems and services in scope, marking which are critical, and record for each the risk rating carried across from the ICT risk management framework, the reasoning behind that rating, and the test priority it produces. Systems deliberately held out of scope are listed with the reason rather than omitted, so the register shows the whole estate. Attach the scope register.

evidenceHint.en: Testing scope register: each ICT system with its critical marking, risk rating, the reasoning, the resulting test priority, and the reason recorded for every exclusion

text.en: List the ICT systems and services in scope, marking each one that is critical.
Carry each system's risk rating across from the ICT risk management framework.
Set the test priority that rating produces and record the reasoning for it.
List the systems held out of scope, with the reason for each exclusion.

title.en: Document the resilience testing programme and how it sits within the ICT risk management framework

description.en: Produce the programme document: what the testing sets out to establish, the test types it uses, how the scope register's risk ratings drive what is tested and in what order, the requirement that tests are performed by independent parties, how findings are prioritised and remediated, and the point at which results feed back into the ICT risk management framework. Name the role accountable for the programme. Attach the issued programme with its version number and issue date.

evidenceHint.en: The issued digital operational resilience testing programme, versioned and dated, covering test types, risk-based prioritisation, tester independence, remediation and the link to the ICT risk management framework

title.en: Build the test plan and schedule assigning each in-scope system a test type and a test window

description.en: Turn the programme into a dated plan. For every entry in the scope register, record the test type it receives, the window within the programme cycle in which it will be tested, the party that will perform it, and the access or environment the test depends on. Show the coverage of critical systems across the cycle explicitly, so a system the plan never reaches is visible while the cycle can still be changed rather than discovered when it ends. Attach the test plan and schedule.

evidenceHint.en: Test plan and schedule: each in-scope system with its test type, test window, performing party, access dependencies, and the coverage view across the programme cycle

title.en: Confirm the independence of the party performing each test before the engagement starts

description.en: Before a test begins, check and record that the party performing it is independent of the team that builds or runs the system under test. Record the testing party, its relationship to the system owner, the criteria checked, the conclusion, and who accepted it; for an external party record the engagement reference so Procurement's contract can be located from the test file. File the confirmation with the test record so each report can be paired with its independence check. The signed confirmations for the period are the evidence.

evidenceHint.en: Signed tester independence confirmation for each test performed in the period, naming the testing party, its relationship to the system owner, the criteria checked and the acceptor

title.en: Track every finding raised by a test from prioritisation through to remediation

description.en: Enter each finding a test produces into the remediation tracker with the test it came from, the system affected, the priority assigned under the programme's prioritisation rules, the named owner, the agreed remediation and its current state. Keep the state current as the work lands, and record the verification that closed each finding rather than closing it on the owner's assertion. The tracker export for the period, showing open and closed findings with their priority and owner, is the artifact attached.

evidenceHint.en: Remediation tracker export for the period: each test finding with its source test, affected system, priority, owner, remediation state and the verification that closed it

title.en: Verify the programme's coverage of critical ICT systems and record the systems not yet tested

description.en: Compare the tests actually performed against the scope register, to see whether coverage of critical systems is being achieved across the cycle rather than only planned. Mark every critical system as tested, scheduled or not reached, and for each not reached record the cause and what changes in the plan. Where a system was tested but its findings remain open past the date agreed in the tracker, record that too — coverage without remediation leaves the risk exactly where the test found it. Attach the coverage review with its conclusions.

evidenceHint.en: Programme coverage review: every critical system marked tested, scheduled or not reached for the cycle, with the cause and plan change per gap and the findings still open past their agreed date

templates.title: Testing of ICT tools and systems
templates.description: Map each ICT system and tool to the test types it must undergo, and schedule at least one test within the year for every critical system in the matrix.
templates.objective: To ensure each ICT system and tool undergoes the test types appropriate to it, and that no critical system passes a year without being tested.
templates.successCriteria:
The matrix gives every ICT system and tool its test types, their prerequisites and the owner who supplies them.
The schedule places at least one test inside the year for every critical ICT system.
Scan reports state the scope actually tested, the tool version, whether the run was authenticated, and findings by severity.
Penetration and scenario-based reports name any in-scope area that could not be tested.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the test-type matrix covering ICT systems and tools with their critical markings and assigned test types.
Collect the dated test schedule for the year with the performing party and agreed window against each test.
Retrieve the vulnerability assessment and scan reports produced in the period.
Gather the penetration test reports and scenario-based test results for every engagement in the schedule.
Obtain the annual coverage check marking each critical system tested, reduced-scope or untested.

Analysis:
Reconcile the matrix against the ICT asset inventory to surface systems and tools carrying no assigned test type at all.
Confirm the scope each scan report says it tested matches the system's matrix entry rather than a narrower slice of it.
Note where a scan ran unauthenticated against a system whose assigned test type calls for credentialled coverage.
Read the penetration and scenario reports for areas recorded as untestable and check whether the obstacle was carried back into the schedule.
Verify the test dates behind each tested marking in the coverage check fall inside the year being claimed.

Output:
An inventory-to-matrix reconciliation naming systems and tools with no assigned test type.
A per-system record of test dates, report references and the test types actually performed.
A gap list of critical systems untested or tested in reduced scope, with the cause and remedy against each.

title.en: Map each ICT system and tool to the test types it must undergo

description.en: Build the matrix that says what kind of testing each system gets — vulnerability assessment, scan, gap analysis, penetration test, scenario-based test — and which combination applies where. Mark the critical ICT systems, which are the ones to be tested at least yearly, and record for each assigned test what it needs in order to run: environment, access, data, and the owner who provides them. A test with no named prerequisite owner is the one that slips. Attach the completed matrix.

evidenceHint.en: Test-type matrix: every ICT system and tool with its critical marking, the test types assigned to it, the prerequisites each test needs and the system owner who provides them

text.en: List every ICT system and tool, marking those identified as critical.
Assign the applicable test types to each system across the range in use.
Record the environment, access and data each assigned test needs to run.
Name the system owner who provides access and prerequisites for each test.

title.en: Schedule at least one test within the year for every critical ICT system in the matrix

description.en: Produce a dated schedule that places at least one test on every critical ICT system within the year, drawing its test type from the matrix, and places the remaining systems according to what the matrix assigns them. Record for each entry the test type, the planned date, the party performing it, and the window agreed with the system owner. Where a critical system cannot be tested within the year, record the obstacle and the interim measure against that entry rather than leaving the slot empty and the gap unstated. Attach the schedule.

evidenceHint.en: Dated test schedule showing at least one test within the year for every critical ICT system, with the test type drawn from the matrix, the performing party, the agreed window, and any obstacle recorded

title.en: Test each scheduled system with a vulnerability assessment or scan and file the resulting report

description.en: Run the vulnerability assessments and scans the schedule calls for, and file the report each produces against the system it covers. A usable report carries the scope actually tested, the date, the tool and its signature or plugin version, whether the scan was authenticated, and the findings with their severity. Where a scheduled scan did not run, or covered less than planned, record that on the report rather than filing nothing — an absent report and a clean one look identical in a folder. The reports for the period are the artifact attached.

evidenceHint.en: Vulnerability assessment and scan reports for the period, each naming the system, the scope actually tested, the date, the tool version, whether it was authenticated, and the findings by severity

title.en: Collect the penetration test and scenario-based test reports for every engagement in the schedule

description.en: For each penetration test and scenario-based test performed, obtain the tester's report and file it against the systems in scope. Check on receipt that it states the scope and the dates tested, the method or scenario used, the findings with their severity, and anything in scope that could not be tested — a report missing those cannot support the conclusion drawn from it, and the time to say so is on receipt. Register the findings so they reach the remediation tracker. Attach the reports for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Penetration test reports and scenario test results for the period, each stating the scope, dates, method or scenario, findings by severity, and any in-scope area that could not be tested

title.en: Verify that every critical ICT system was tested within the last year and record those that were not

description.en: Check the filed reports against the test-type matrix and the schedule to establish that each critical ICT system has been tested within the last year, recording which of the test types the matrix assigns it were performed. Mark every critical system as tested, tested with reduced scope, or not tested, giving the date and report reference for those tested and the cause and remedy for those not. Attach the coverage check: it is what demonstrates the yearly testing of critical systems actually happened, rather than that it was planned.

evidenceHint.en: Annual coverage check listing each critical ICT system as tested, reduced-scope or untested, with the test date, report reference and test types performed for each, and the cause and remedy for every gap

templates.title: Threat-led penetration testing (TLPT)
templates.description: Record whether threat-led penetration testing applies to the entity, and scope each exercise to the critical or important functions it must cover.
templates.objective: To ensure threat-led penetration testing, where it binds the entity, exercises critical or important functions on live production systems and ends in an authority attestation.
templates.successCriteria:
A signed determination records whether threat-led testing binds the entity, on what basis and by whom.
The approved scope names the critical or important functions, their live production systems and the previous test date.
Each completed test has a filed report carrying its completion date and the functions exercised.
An attestation by authorities is held per test, with its request and receipt dates.
Every finding sits in the remediation plan with an owner and a closure status.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the signed in-scope determination with the decision-maker and date recorded on it.
Collect the approved TLPT scope document for each exercise in the period.
Retrieve the report filed for every completed threat-led test.
Gather the attestations by authorities held against those reports.
Export the TLPT remediation plan.

Analysis:
Test the determination's stated basis against the entity's own profile rather than accepting the conclusion on its own.
Compare the functions listed in the scope document with the entity's register of critical or important functions and note any omission.
Confirm the systems named in scope are live production systems and not a staging or mirrored equivalent.
Read each report's covered functions against the approved scope and identify where the test delivered less than it was scoped for.
Measure the interval between the previous test date and this one, and check each attestation's receipt date follows the completion it certifies.

Output:
A scope-to-coverage comparison for each completed test.
A register of tests with completion dates and attestation request and receipt dates.
An open-findings list drawn from the remediation plan with the owner named against each.

title.en: Record the threat-led penetration testing in-scope determination for the entity

description.en: TLPT applies to identified financial entities, so the first deliverable is the written determination: whether this entity has been identified as in scope, on what basis, who made the determination and when. Where the entity is in scope, record who identified it and the notification that conveyed it if one exists; where it is not, record the basis so the position can be re-taken when the entity's profile changes. Attach the signed determination.

evidenceHint.en: Signed TLPT in-scope determination naming the basis for the conclusion, the decision-maker and the date

title.en: Produce the TLPT scope document covering the critical or important functions and their live production systems

description.en: Write the TLPT scope document this control names as evidence: the critical or important functions the test must cover, the live production systems and services supporting each of them, the threat-led scenarios the test will follow, and the date of the previous test, so the interval against the at-least-every-three-years frequency the article sets is visible before this scope is approved. Derive the function list from the entity's own critical-function register rather than restating the article. Attach the scope document together with its approval.

evidenceHint.en: Approved TLPT scope document listing the critical or important functions, the live production systems in scope and the date of the previous test

text.en: Pull the critical or important functions from the entity's own register.
Map each function to the live production systems and services supporting it.
Set out the threat-led scenarios the test will follow and where they came from.
Record the date of the previous TLPT and the interval this test closes.
Obtain and attach the approval of the scope before any testing begins.

title.en: File the TLPT report for each completed test with its completion date and the functions covered

description.en: When a test completes, file the TLPT report together with the start and completion dates and the list of critical or important functions the test actually exercised — which can differ from the scoped list. Those dates are what lets anyone read the interval between successive tests against the at-least-every-three-years frequency the article sets, so record them on the report itself and not only in a calendar.

evidenceHint.en: TLPT report per completed test, carrying the completion date and the critical or important functions the test exercised

title.en: Obtain the authority attestation for each completed TLPT and file it against the report

description.en: Request and retain the attestation the authorities issue for a completed TLPT, filing it against the report it attests. Record the date the attestation was requested and the date it was received; where one is outstanding, keep the request open rather than closing the test out. This artifact is what shows an external party accepted the exercise as a TLPT, not merely that a test happened.

evidenceHint.en: Attestation by authorities for each completed TLPT, filed with its report and carrying the request and receipt dates

title.en: Track every TLPT finding to closure in the TLPT remediation plan

description.en: Open the remediation plan from the report's findings: one row per finding, carrying the affected function, the owner, the remediation agreed and its current status. Close a row only against evidence that the fix landed, and carry any finding still open into the scope of the next test. Attach the remediation plan showing the status of every finding.

evidenceHint.en: TLPT remediation plan showing each finding, its owner, the remediation agreed and its closure status

templates.title: TLPT tester suitability and independence
templates.description: Set the suitability, independence, certification and indemnity criteria a TLPT tester must meet, and hold the due-diligence evidence showing a given tester meets them.
templates.objective: To ensure every tester engaged on a threat-led penetration test is demonstrably suitable, independent of what is being tested, certified and covered by indemnity.
templates.successCriteria:
The criteria set says what counts as meeting each suitability, independence, certification and indemnity requirement.
The evidence request maps every criterion to the document that proves it.
Each engaged tester holds a due-diligence record against every criterion, with its conclusion and author.
Independence records name each tester's relationships to the in-scope teams and systems, plus any restriction imposed.
Certification and indemnity cover are on file with periods spanning the test dates.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the versioned tester criteria set.
Collect the due-diligence evidence request showing the criterion-to-document mapping.
Retrieve the due-diligence record completed for each tester engaged in the period.
Gather the independence assessments raised for each engagement.
Obtain the certification or accreditation documents and the professional indemnity evidence held per tester.

Analysis:
Check that each criterion carries a stated threshold rather than a bare requirement, and that the evidence request reaches all of them.
Inspect the documents received for a sample of criteria and confirm their dates precede the engagement they support.
Examine criteria marked met only in part for a recorded conclusion explaining why the tester was engaged regardless.
Test each independence record against the teams and systems the scope document places inside the test, and confirm any restriction imposed was carried into the engagement.
Compare the period of each indemnity policy and certification with the test dates it is relied on to cover.

Output:
A per-tester file completeness table set against the criteria.
A note on criteria met in part and the reasoning accepted for each.
A list of engagements where a document was missing, expired or received only after the test began.

title.en: Set out the suitability, independence, certification and indemnity criteria a TLPT tester must meet

description.en: Write the criteria set that every prospective threat-led penetration testing provider is assessed against, so an engagement decision is decidable rather than a judgement made under time pressure. Cover the suitability and reputation the entity requires, the independence it requires from the teams that build, run and defend the systems inside a TLPT scope, the professional-ethics standard or code of conduct the tester adheres to, the certification or accreditation held, and the professional indemnity cover in force. For each criterion record what would count as meeting it, so two assessors applying the set reach the same answer. Attach the criteria set with its version and issue date.

evidenceHint.en: The TLPT tester criteria set, versioned and dated: each suitability, reputation, independence, professional-ethics, certification or accreditation and indemnity criterion with what counts as meeting it

text.en: Record the suitability and reputation criteria a prospective TLPT tester has to meet.
State the independence required from the teams that build, run and defend in-scope systems.
Record the professional-ethics standard and the certification or accreditation expected.
Record the professional indemnity cover the entity requires to be in force.
For each criterion, state the bar an assessor applies to decide it is met.

title.en: Build the due-diligence evidence request that maps each tester criterion to the document proving it

description.en: Turn the criteria set into the pack that goes to a prospective TLPT tester. For each criterion name the document that would prove it — the certification or accreditation certificate, the professional indemnity policy or certificate of cover, the statement of the code of conduct or ethical framework adhered to, and the references or engagement history supporting reputation — and state what the assessor checks on each: that it names the tester being engaged, that it is current, and that it covers the work in question. Record who assesses the returned pack and where the completed record is filed against the engagement. Attach the issued request with its version.

evidenceHint.en: The tester due-diligence evidence request, versioned, mapping every criterion to the document that proves it, what the assessor checks on each, and where the completed record is filed

text.en: Name the document that proves each criterion in the tester criteria set.
State what the assessor checks on each document received back.
Record who assesses the returned pack and where the record is filed.
Record how a criterion answered only in part is to be written down.

title.en: Complete a due-diligence record for every tester engaged on a TLPT and file it with the engagement

description.en: For each TLPT tester engaged in the period, run the evidence request, record the assessment against each criterion, note the documents received and their dates, and record the conclusion reached and who reached it. Where a criterion is met only in part, or the document supplied does not cover the work being engaged, record that against the criterion rather than folding it into the overall conclusion — a partial answer absorbed into a pass is the one nobody can find afterwards. File the completed record against the engagement so the tester file can be reached from the TLPT report. The due-diligence records for the period are the evidence attached.

evidenceHint.en: Tester due-diligence records for the period: per tester the assessment against each criterion, the documents received with their dates, any criterion met only in part, and the conclusion with who reached it

title.en: Assess each TLPT tester's independence from the teams and systems inside the test scope

description.en: Independence is specific to what is being tested, so it is assessed against the scope of the engagement rather than settled once for the tester. For each TLPT engagement record the testing provider and the individuals proposed, the relationship each has to the teams that build, run or defend the systems in the TLPT scope — prior engagements on those systems, group ownership, and any advisory work — the criteria applied from the criteria set, the conclusion reached, and who reached it. Where a relationship exists and the engagement proceeds anyway, record the reasoning and any restriction placed on the tester, so the decision is legible later. Attach the independence assessment for each engagement.

evidenceHint.en: Independence assessment per TLPT engagement: the testing provider and proposed individuals, their relationships to the in-scope teams and systems, the criteria applied, the conclusion, who reached it, and any restriction imposed

text.en: List the testing provider and the individuals proposed for the engagement.
Record each one's relationship to the teams that build, run or defend in-scope systems.
Apply the independence criteria and record the conclusion and who reached it.
Where a relationship exists, record the reasoning and any restriction placed on the tester.

title.en: File the certification or accreditation and the professional indemnity cover held by each TLPT tester

description.en: Keep the documents themselves, not a note that somebody saw them. For each engaged tester file the certification or accreditation document naming the body that issued it and the period it runs for, and the professional indemnity evidence naming the insurer, the cover provided and the period it runs for. On filing, check that each names the tester actually engaged rather than a parent or an affiliate, and record whether its period spans the dates of the test so any gap is visible on the file rather than reconstructed later. Where a document lapses while an engagement is running, note that against the file so it is chased. The filed certificates and cover evidence for the period are the artifact attached.

evidenceHint.en: Certification or accreditation documents and professional indemnity evidence on file per TLPT tester, each naming the tester engaged, its issuing body or insurer, and its period recorded against the test dates

title.en: Re-check that each TLPT run in the period was performed by a tester with a complete and current file

description.en: Take the TLPTs performed in the period and pair each with its tester file. For every one, confirm that a due-diligence record, an independence assessment and the certification and indemnity evidence are all present, that each was made against the criteria set in force at the time, and that nothing on file had lapsed before the test finished. Mark each engagement complete or deficient, and for every deficiency record the cause — a document never chased, an independence assessment made against a different scope, a criterion the set does not in fact make decidable — and the correction it calls for. Attach the completed check with the engagement list it was made from.

evidenceHint.en: Tester file check for the period: each TLPT engagement marked complete or deficient against its due-diligence, independence and certification and indemnity records, with the cause and correction for every deficiency

text.en: List the TLPT engagements performed in the period and pair each with its tester file.
Confirm the due-diligence, independence and certification and indemnity records are present.
Check each was made against the criteria set in force at the time of the engagement.
Record the cause and correction for every engagement marked deficient.

templates.title: ICT third-party risk strategy and Register of Information
templates.description: Compile the Register of Information covering every contractual arrangement for the use of ICT services, and adopt the third-party risk strategy governing how such arrangements are entered and exited.
templates.objective: To ensure every arrangement for the use of ICT services is registered and kept current, and that entering and leaving such arrangements follows an adopted strategy.
templates.successCriteria:
The Register of Information carries every ICT arrangement with its provider, service, function and dates.
An approved third-party risk strategy is in force, multi-vendor position included, with a dated approval record.
Each ICT service behind a critical or important function has an exit plan with triggers, data return and owner.
No arrangement was entered or renewed without a pre-contract risk assessment carrying a decision to proceed.
Signatures, amendments and closures reach the register change log on the date they happen.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the Register of Information as it stands at the review date.
Collect the adopted third-party risk strategy and multi-vendor strategy with their approval records.
Retrieve the exit plan held for each ICT service supporting a critical or important function.
Gather the pre-contract ICT risk assessments for arrangements entered or renewed in the period.
Export the register change log and the reconciliation record raised against contracts and spend.

Analysis:
Reconcile the register against the contract repository and the ICT supplier spend ledger, looking both ways.
Confirm every critical or important function named in the register has an exit plan whose owner is still in post.
Check each pre-contract assessment carries an explicit decision to proceed and an author, and predates the arrangement it approved.
Check that arrangements signed, amended or ended in the period show up in the change log rather than only in the register.
Read the multi-vendor position in the strategy against the provider spread the register actually shows.

Output:
A reconciliation listing arrangements held but unregistered and registered but no longer held.
A coverage table of exit plans against ICT services supporting critical or important functions.
A list of arrangements entered without a pre-contract risk assessment, or ahead of one.

title.en: Compile the Register of Information covering every contractual arrangement for the use of ICT services

description.en: Build the register this article requires: one row per contractual arrangement for the use of ICT services, whatever its size or label — cloud service, software subscription, managed service, intra-group arrangement. For each, record the provider, the ICT service supplied, the business function it supports, whether that function is critical or important, the contract dates and the internal owner. Source the population from procurement and finance records rather than from team recall, so an arrangement nobody sponsors still appears. Attach the register.

evidenceHint.en: Register of Information listing every ICT service contractual arrangement with its provider, the service supplied, the function supported and the contract dates

text.en: Pull the supplier population from procurement and finance records, not team recall.
Record the ICT service supplied and the function it supports for each arrangement.
Flag the arrangements that support a critical or important function.
Record the contract start, renewal and end dates on every row.
Name the internal owner accountable for each arrangement.

title.en: Adopt the ICT third-party risk strategy, including the multi-vendor position

description.en: Take the ICT third-party risk strategy through the entity's own approval route and record who adopted it and when — the article requires the strategy, not a particular approver. It should state how ICT third-party risk is managed as part of the wider ICT risk framework, the entity's position on using more than one vendor for the same ICT service, and the conditions under which an ICT service supporting a critical or important function may be placed with a provider at all. Attach the adopted strategy together with the approval record.

evidenceHint.en: Adopted ICT third-party risk strategy and multi-vendor strategy, with the approval record naming the date and the approver

title.en: Write an exit plan for each ICT service supporting a critical or important function

description.en: For every arrangement flagged critical or important in the Register of Information, produce an exit plan: the conditions that would trigger exit, the steps to move or repatriate the service, the data return and deletion route, any transitional support available under the contract, and the internal owner of the plan. A plan naming no owner and no steps is a statement of intent, not an exit plan. Attach one plan per critical arrangement.

evidenceHint.en: Exit plan per critical or important ICT service, naming the exit triggers, the transition steps, the data return route and the plan owner

title.en: Record the pre-contract ICT risk assessment for each new or renewed ICT arrangement

description.en: Before an ICT contractual arrangement is entered or renewed, complete and file the risk assessment this article expects: the ICT service, the function it supports, the risks identified, the mitigations relied on, and the decision to proceed with the name of whoever took it. Where an assessment is not performed because the arrangement is judged out of scope, record that judgement in the same place — an absent assessment and a considered exclusion must be told apart. Attach the period's assessments.

evidenceHint.en: Pre-contract ICT risk assessments for the period, one per new or renewed arrangement, each carrying the decision to proceed and its author

title.en: Update the Register of Information whenever an ICT arrangement is signed, changed or ended

description.en: Wire register maintenance into the contract lifecycle so the register stays current between reviews: a new signature adds a row, an amendment updates it, a termination closes it with the end date and the exit route taken. Keep the change log alongside so a reader can see when each row last moved and who moved it. Attach the change log for the period together with the current register.

evidenceHint.en: Register of Information change log for the period showing each addition, amendment and closure with its date and author

title.en: Reconcile the Register of Information against the ICT contracts actually held

description.en: Compare the register against the contract population held by procurement and the ICT spend recorded by finance. Record arrangements present in one source and missing from the other, decide which record is correct, and correct it. Report the number of rows reconciled alongside the discrepancies found, so the register's completeness is a measured claim rather than an assumed one.

evidenceHint.en: Register of Information reconciliation record listing the discrepancies found against contract and spend records, and how each was resolved

templates.title: ICT concentration-risk assessment
templates.description: Group the ICT arrangements supporting critical or important functions by provider, and assess concentration risk by a stated method before contracting rather than after.
templates.objective: To ensure the entity knows where dependence on a single ICT provider or supply chain concentrates, and judges that concentration by a stated method before it contracts.
templates.successCriteria:
The provider-to-function view shows what each ICT provider supports and the arrangements behind it.
An approved method names the factors examined, the evidence requested from providers and the sign-off.
Every critical-function arrangement holds a concentration assessment dated ahead of contract signature.
Each critical provider's declared sub-contractors are recorded against the part of the service they perform.
Each critical-function provider carries a current view of whether an alternative exists.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the provider-to-function view covering critical and important functions.
Collect the approved concentration-risk assessment method with its sign-off.
Retrieve the concentration assessments completed for arrangements entered in the period.
Gather the sub-outsourcing analyses declared by providers of critical or important functions.
Obtain the substitutability analysis held per critical-function provider.

Analysis:
